useCases.title: Elasticsearch Fielddata and Cache Evictions
useCases.value: Fielddata evictions force expensive re-computation of in-memory data structures, causing search latency spikes. Query cache evictions reduce the benefit of repeated queries. Tracking eviction rates guides memory tuning.

useCases.title: Elasticsearch Segment Merge Pressure
useCases.value: Heavy segment merge activity competes with search for disk I/O, causing latency spikes. Merge throttling slows indexing. Monitoring merge pressure helps balance indexing throughput against search performance.

useCases.title: Solr Core Admin Health
useCases.value: Core-level errors (recovery failures, corrupt index flags, leader election issues) degrade search for specific collections; admin health checks catch per-core problems early.

useCases.title: Elasticsearch Ingest Pipeline Error Rate
useCases.value: Ingest pipeline failures silently drop or corrupt documents before indexing. Monitoring error rates per pipeline ensures data quality and completeness.

useCases.title: Database Connection Pool Utilization Trending
useCases.value: Peak connection pool utilization over 30 days shows how close applications are to exhausting database sessions. Rising peaks justify pool tuning, connection string fixes, or server scale-up before login storms cause outages.

useCases.title: Slow Query Volume Trending
useCases.value: Counting queries exceeding a duration threshold per day quantifies database pain for developers and DBAs. Upward trends after releases often indicate missing indexes or plan regressions before p95 latency alerts fire.

useCases.title: Replication Lag Trending
useCases.value: Maximum and average replication lag by replica over 30 days validates disaster-recovery readiness and read-consistency expectations. Gradual lag growth can signal network, disk, or write-volume problems before replica promotion fails.

useCases.title: Database Backup Size Trending
useCases.value: Monthly backup size growth forecasts storage for backup appliances and cloud object storage costs. Anomalous jumps can indicate bulk data loads, failed truncations, or ransomware preparation worth investigating.

useCases.title: Index Fragmentation Trending
useCases.value: Average fragmentation percentage over 30 days guides `REBUILD`/`REORG` scheduling and fill-factor reviews. Slow upward trends on hot tables correlate with extra I/O and slower queries even when CPU looks healthy.

useCases.title: HTTP Error Rate Monitoring
useCases.value: Rising error rates signal application issues, backend failures, or attacks. Rapid detection reduces user impact and MTTR.

useCases.title: Response Time Trending
useCases.value: Increasing response times degrade user experience before complete failures occur. Trending enables proactive optimization.

useCases.title: Request Rate Trending
useCases.value: Traffic trending supports capacity planning and identifies unexpected traffic patterns (bot attacks, viral events, traffic drops).

useCases.title: Top Error URIs
useCases.value: Identifies the most problematic endpoints for targeted developer attention. Reduces noise by focusing on high-impact errors.

useCases.title: SSL Certificate Monitoring
useCases.value: Expired SSL certificates cause complete service outage and browser security warnings. Proactive monitoring prevents this entirely avoidable failure.

useCases.title: Upstream Backend Health
useCases.value: Backend server failures behind reverse proxies cause partial service degradation. Detection enables rapid failover response.

useCases.title: Bot and Crawler Detection
useCases.value: Bot traffic inflates metrics and consumes resources. Identification enables accurate capacity planning and bot management policies.

useCases.title: Connection Pool Saturation
useCases.value: Saturated worker threads/processes cause request queuing and timeouts. Monitoring enables proactive scaling.

useCases.title: Slow POST Detection
useCases.value: Slow POST requests often indicate application-level performance issues (large form submissions, file uploads, database writes) distinct from slow GETs.

useCases.title: Configuration Reload Tracking
useCases.value: Configuration changes are a common cause of outages. Tracking reloads enables rapid correlation with incidents.

useCases.title: NGINX Upstream Response Errors
useCases.value: Counts upstream HTTP 5xx and connect/timeout errors from NGINX access/error logs. Isolates reverse-proxy vs origin issues faster than aggregate 5xx alone.

useCases.title: Apache mod_security WAF Blocks
useCases.value: Tracks ModSecurity rule IDs and scores for blocked requests. Supports tuning false positives and detecting attack campaigns.

useCases.title: IIS Worker Process Recycling
useCases.value: Frequent `w3wp` recycles cause session loss and latency spikes. Event Log IDs 5074, 5002, 1011 indicate config, memory, or crash-driven recycles.

useCases.title: SSL Certificate Expiry Countdown
useCases.value: Days-to-expiry dashboard for all TLS endpoints monitored by cert checks. Complements UC-8.1.5 with trend and earliest-expiry focus.

useCases.title: HAProxy Backend Health State
useCases.value: CSV stats `status` (UP/DOWN/MAINT) per server line with weight. Distinct from UC-8.1.6 NGINX-only upstream errors for HAProxy-native shops.

useCases.title: Web Server Thread Pool Exhaustion
useCases.value: IIS `QueueFull`, NGINX worker saturation, or Apache `BusyWorkers` at limit causes queueing. Unified thresholding across stacks.

useCases.title: IIS Web Server Monitoring
useCases.value: IIS access logs provide visibility into web application health — error rates, response times, and request volumes. Critical for web-facing services.

useCases.title: IIS Application Pool Crashes & Recycling
useCases.value: Application pool crashes cause HTTP 503 errors and service outages. Frequent recycling indicates memory leaks or configuration issues in web applications.

useCases.title: JVM Heap Utilization
useCases.value: JVM heap exhaustion causes OutOfMemoryError, crashing the application. Monitoring enables tuning before failures occur.

useCases.title: Garbage Collection Impact
useCases.value: Frequent or long GC pauses cause application latency spikes and request timeouts. Monitoring guides JVM tuning.

useCases.title: Thread Pool Exhaustion
useCases.value: Exhausted thread pools cause request rejection and application unresponsiveness. Detection prevents complete service failure.

useCases.title: Application Error Rate
useCases.value: Application exceptions indicate bugs, integration failures, or environmental issues. Tracking error rate by type guides debugging priority.

useCases.title: Deployment Tracking
useCases.value: Correlating deployments with performance changes is the fastest way to identify deployment-caused regressions. Essential for change management.

useCases.title: Connection Pool Monitoring
useCases.value: Exhausted JDBC/database connection pools cause application errors and cascading failures. Monitoring prevents connection starvation.

useCases.title: Session Count Trending
useCases.value: Active session counts indicate concurrent user load. Trending supports capacity planning and license management.

useCases.title: .NET CLR Performance
useCases.value: CLR performance issues (high GC, exceptions, thread starvation) directly impact .NET application performance. Monitoring guides runtime tuning.

useCases.title: Node.js Event Loop Lag
useCases.value: Event loop lag indicates blocking operations that prevent Node.js from handling requests. Detection enables code-level investigation.

useCases.title: Class Loading Issues
useCases.value: ClassNotFoundException and NoClassDefFoundError indicate deployment or dependency issues that may cause intermittent failures.

useCases.title: PHP-FPM Pool Monitoring
useCases.value: Active/idle process counts, listen queue depth, and slow request detection indicate PHP-FPM capacity and backend saturation. Exhausted pools cause 502 errors and request timeouts.

useCases.title: Tomcat JMX Thread Pool Utilization
useCases.value: Connector thread pool busy percentage and rejected connections indicate Tomcat capacity limits. Exhausted pools cause 503 errors and connection timeouts.

useCases.title: WildFly / JBoss Datasource Pool Usage
useCases.value: JMX datasource pool active/idle/wait connections indicate database connectivity health. Exhausted pools cause application errors and slow transactions.

useCases.title: JVM Garbage Collection Pause Time (STW)
useCases.value: Stop-the-world pause duration percentiles from unified GC logs (G1, ZGC) drive SLA breaches before heap % alerts fire.

useCases.title: .NET CLR Memory Pressure
useCases.value: `# Bytes in all Heaps`, `LOH` size, and `% Time in GC` together indicate memory pressure vs high allocation rate. Refines UC-8.2.8.

useCases.title: Node.js Event Loop Lag (High Resolution)
useCases.value: `eventLoopUtilization` and `delay` histogram from `perf_hooks` or Prometheus `nodejs_eventloop_lag_seconds` for sub-millisecond vs millisecond precision.

useCases.title: Python WSGI Worker Pool Exhaustion
useCases.value: Gunicorn/uWSGI `active workers`, `listening queue`, and `timeout` worker kills indicate saturation or slow upstream (DB).

useCases.title: Tomcat Active Session Count
useCases.value: Session explosion may indicate bot traffic, session fixation abuse, or missing session TTL. Per-context session counts from JMX.

useCases.title: WebLogic Stuck Threads
useCases.value: Stuck thread count >0 blocks request processing and triggers health check failures. Server log `BEA-000337` patterns.

useCases.title: JBoss / WildFly Deployment Failures
useCases.value: Failed deployments leave apps stopped or partial. Log markers `WFLYSRV0026`, `Deployment FAILED` require immediate attention.

useCases.title: Spring Boot Actuator Health Down
useCases.value: `/actuator/health` JSON with `status:DOWN` from liveness/readiness probes. Aggregates component failures (diskSpace, db, redis).

useCases.title: .NET Exception Rate Trending
useCases.value: `# of Exceps Thrown / sec` and first-chance exception logs show error storms after deploys. Complements log-based UC-8.2.4 with runtime counters.

useCases.title: Jira Data Center Performance
useCases.value: JMX metrics, request duration, and attachment storage indicate Jira health. Slow requests frustrate users; disk usage growth risks outages. Enables capacity planning and performance tuning.

useCases.title: Consumer Lag Monitoring
useCases.value: Growing consumer lag means messages aren't being processed fast enough, leading to data staleness and eventual message loss if retention is exceeded.

useCases.title: Queue Depth Trending
useCases.value: Growing queue depths indicate consumers can't keep up or are down. Trending prevents message loss and processing delays.

useCases.title: Broker Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Broker failures cause message loss and application disruption. Health monitoring ensures cluster stability.

useCases.title: Under-Replicated Partitions
useCases.value: Under-replicated partitions mean data is at risk of loss if additional brokers fail. Immediate remediation is required.

useCases.title: Dead Letter Queue Monitoring
useCases.value: Messages in DLQ represent processing failures that need investigation. They may indicate bugs, schema changes, or downstream failures.

useCases.title: Message Throughput Trending
useCases.value: Throughput trending identifies capacity limits and validates scaling decisions. Unexpected drops indicate producer or broker issues.

useCases.title: Topic/Queue Creation Audit
useCases.value: Uncontrolled topic/queue creation can lead to resource sprawl. Audit trail supports governance and cleanup.

useCases.title: Consumer Group Rebalancing
useCases.value: Frequent rebalances cause processing pauses and duplicate message delivery. Detection identifies unstable consumers.

useCases.title: Partition Leader Elections
useCases.value: Frequent leader elections indicate broker instability, causing temporary unavailability for affected partitions.

useCases.title: Message Age Monitoring
useCases.value: Old messages in queues indicate processing delays that may violate SLAs. Age tracking provides a business-relevant metric beyond raw queue depth.

useCases.title: RabbitMQ Queue Monitoring
useCases.value: Queue depth, consumer count, message rate, and unacknowledged messages indicate message processing health. Growing depth or unacked messages signal consumer lag or failures.

useCases.title: ZooKeeper Ensemble Health
useCases.value: Leader election state, outstanding requests, and watch count indicate ZooKeeper stability. Frequent leader changes or growing outstanding requests signal ensemble instability affecting Kafka, HBase, and other dependents.

useCases.title: Kafka Consumer Lag Monitoring (Consumer Group)
useCases.value: Lag in messages and approximate time lag per partition for each `group.id`. Tightens UC-8.3.1 with `kafka-consumer-groups` export fields.

useCases.title: RabbitMQ Queue Depth Alerts
useCases.value: Per-queue `messages_ready` thresholds with business priority tags. Alert routing by `queue` name pattern (`critical.*`).

useCases.title: Azure Service Bus Dead Letter Monitoring
useCases.value: DLQ message count per topic/subscription and dead-letter reasons (`DeliveryCount`, `ExceptionDescription`) for cloud-native messaging.

useCases.title: Kafka Connect Task Failures
useCases.value: Connector `FAILED` state, task failures, and `offset_commit` errors stop data pipelines. Distinct from broker-only monitoring.

useCases.title: Kafka Topic Partition Skew
useCases.value: Byte size and message count skew across partitions causes hot brokers and uneven consumer lag. Uses `kafka-log-dirs` or broker metrics.

useCases.title: RabbitMQ Memory Alarm
useCases.value: `mem_alarm` blocks publishers when `vm_memory_high_watermark` is hit. Early warning from `memory` and `allocated` fields.

useCases.title: ActiveMQ Broker Store Usage
useCases.value: Persistent store percent used (KahaDB) or JDBC store growth causes broker pause and producer blocking. JMX `StoreLimit` usage.

useCases.title: NATS JetStream Consumer Ack Lag
useCases.value: `NumAckPending`, `NumRedelivered`, and consumer lag for JetStream streams indicate slow consumers or poison messages.

useCases.title: MSMQ Queue Depth Monitoring
useCases.value: Message queue buildup indicates application processing failures. Monitoring queue depth prevents message loss and detects downstream system outages.

useCases.title: API Error Rate by Endpoint
useCases.value: Per-endpoint error rates pinpoint failing services, enabling targeted debugging rather than broad investigation.

useCases.title: API Latency Percentiles
useCases.value: P95/P99 latency reveals the experience of the slowest users. Averages hide tail latency problems.

useCases.title: Rate Limiting Events
useCases.value: Rate limiting indicates consumers exceeding their quotas. May signal API abuse, misconfigured clients, or quota adjustments needed.

useCases.title: Authentication Failures
useCases.value: Authentication failures may indicate credential compromise, API key rotation issues, or brute-force attacks.

useCases.title: Service-to-Service Call Failures
useCases.value: Inter-service communication failures in microservices architectures cascade quickly. Detection enables rapid isolation of failing services.

useCases.title: Circuit Breaker Activations
useCases.value: Circuit breaker trips indicate a downstream service is failing. Quick detection enables proactive communication and remediation.

useCases.title: API Consumer Usage Tracking
useCases.value: Usage tracking per API consumer enables billing, quota management, and partner relationship management.

useCases.title: mTLS Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Expired mTLS certificates break service-to-service communication, causing complete mesh failures. Proactive monitoring is essential.

useCases.title: HAProxy Backend and Frontend Health
useCases.value: Backend server state, connection queue depth, and HTTP response distribution indicate load balancer effectiveness and backend capacity. Detection of DOWN backends or saturated queues enables rapid failover and scaling decisions.

useCases.title: Kong Rate Limit Violations
useCases.value: Kong `rate_limiting` plugin log lines and `429` with `RateLimit-*` headers. Identifies abusive consumers vs tight quotas.

useCases.title: AWS API Gateway 4xx/5xx Trends
useCases.value: CloudWatch `4XXError`, `5XXError`, `Latency` per API stage. Single pane for serverless API frontends.

useCases.title: Apigee Policy Violations
useCases.value: Apigee analytics API or syslog with `fault` policy name (SOAPThreat, JSONThreat, Quota, SpikeArrest) for blocked requests.

useCases.title: API Response Time SLA Breaches
useCases.value: p95/p99 latency from gateway access logs vs documented SLA per route (`/api/v1/orders`). Complements UC-8.4.2 with SLA lookup join.

app: Gateway logs with consumer_id or api_key hash
useCases.title: API Key Abuse Detection
useCases.value: Unusual volume of requests per API key or key used from many distinct IPs/countries in short window.

useCases.title: GraphQL Query Depth Violations
useCases.value: Depth/complexity limit errors from Apollo/GraphQL server logs prevent DoS via deep queries.

useCases.title: API Version Deprecation Tracking
useCases.value: Traffic to `/v1/` deprecated routes vs `/v2/` for migration planning. Header `Sunset` or path-based routing logs.

useCases.title: Cache Hit/Miss Ratio
useCases.value: Cache hit ratio directly measures cache effectiveness. Declining ratio means more backend load and higher latency.

useCases.title: Memory Utilization
useCases.value: Cache memory exhaustion triggers evictions, degrading performance. Monitoring enables timely scaling.

useCases.title: Eviction Rate Trending
useCases.value: High eviction rates mean the cache is too small, causing frequent backend roundtrips. Tracking guides capacity decisions.

useCases.title: Connection Count Monitoring
useCases.value: Approaching connection limits causes client rejections. Monitoring enables proactive limit adjustment.

useCases.title: Replication Lag (Redis)
useCases.value: Redis replication lag affects read consistency for apps reading from replicas. Monitoring ensures data freshness.

useCases.title: Slow Command Detection
useCases.value: Slow Redis commands block the single-threaded event loop, impacting all clients. Detection enables command optimization.

useCases.title: Key Expiration Trending
useCases.value: Monitoring TTL patterns ensures cache freshness strategy is working. Unusual patterns may indicate application bugs.

useCases.title: Memcached Hit Ratio and Eviction Rate
useCases.value: Cache hit ratio and eviction rate measure cache effectiveness and capacity pressure. Declining hit ratio or rising evictions indicate undersized cache or changing access patterns.

useCases.title: Squid Proxy Cache Hit Ratio
useCases.value: Cache HIT/MISS/DENY rates on forward/reverse proxy indicate cache effectiveness and upstream load. Declining ratio increases origin latency and bandwidth.

useCases.title: Varnish Cache Hit Rate and Backend Health
useCases.value: Cache efficiency and backend connection failures indicate Varnish health. Backend failures cause cache misses and user-facing errors.

useCases.title: Synthetic Transaction Monitoring
useCases.value: Simulated multi-step user journeys with timing per step validate end-to-end availability and detect degradation before users report issues. Step-level timing enables pinpointing of slow components.

useCases.title: Website Page Load Time Breakdown
useCases.value: DNS, connect, TLS, TTFB, and download timing per page element enable root cause analysis of slow page loads. Breakdown identifies whether slowness is network, backend, or resource-related.

useCases.title: SSH Service Availability Monitoring
useCases.value: SSH is the primary remote administration channel for Linux and Unix servers. An unresponsive SSH daemon locks out operators and often signals broader system distress (OOM, hung kernel, storage full). Nagios `check_ssh` is one of the most universally deployed checks; Splunk replicates it through absence-of-event detection and syslog-based availability trending.

useCases.title: FTP / SFTP Service Availability Monitoring
useCases.value: FTP and SFTP services support automated file transfer workflows between systems, partners, and legacy integrations. Silent service failures cause missed file deliveries that may not surface until business processes fail downstream. Nagios `check_ftp` provides port-level verification; Splunk replicates this through daemon log monitoring and scripted probes.

useCases.title: Envoy Proxy Upstream Health
useCases.value: Upstream cluster health, retry rate, and circuit breaker trips indicate Envoy proxy and backend service health. Detection enables rapid isolation of failing upstreams.

useCases.title: HashiCorp Vault Seal Status and Token Count
useCases.value: Vault health, auto-unseal events, and token creation rate indicate secrets management availability. Sealed Vault blocks all secret access; token anomalies may indicate abuse.

useCases.title: HashiCorp Consul Service Health
useCases.value: Service registration, deregistration, and health check failures indicate Consul service discovery health. Critical checks mean services are unavailable for discovery and routing.

useCases.title: HashiCorp Nomad Job and Allocation Status
useCases.value: Failed allocations and job deployment health indicate Nomad scheduler and workload availability. Failed allocations mean tasks are not running; deployment failures block rollouts.

useCases.title: Asterisk / FreePBX Call Quality and Trunk Status
useCases.value: Call volume, ASR (Answer Seizure Ratio), ACD (Average Call Duration), and trunk registration indicate VoIP/PBX health. Trunk failures block inbound/outbound calls; quality metrics affect user experience.

useCases.title: NTP Stratum Drift
useCases.value: Stratum jumps or large offset indicate bad upstream clock or local drift — affects Kerberos, TLS, and distributed logs.

useCases.title: DNS Recursive Query Volume
useCases.value: Sudden spike in recursive queries on internal resolvers may indicate DDoS, malware, or misconfigured application loops.

useCases.title: TFTP Unauthorized Access
useCases.value: TFTP should be rare in enterprise networks. Any RRQ/WRQ outside PXE scope may indicate data exfil or firmware abuse.

useCases.title: SNMP Community String Audit
useCases.value: Detects use of default `public`/`private` or unauthorized SNMP GETs to network devices for SNMPv2c exposure auditing.

useCases.title: User Session Volume Trending
useCases.value: Daily or weekly active session counts show adoption, campaign effects, and capacity needs before saturation. Seasonal patterns become visible for staffing and infrastructure scale plans.

useCases.title: API Endpoint Latency Percentile Trending
useCases.value: p50, p95, and p99 latency over 30 days highlights tail latency regressions that averages hide. Trends support SLO setting and regression detection after releases.

useCases.title: Application Error Budget Burn Rate Trending
useCases.value: Error budget remaining over a sprint or month shows whether reliability goals are sustainable. Accelerating burn triggers freeze or rollback decisions before users experience widespread outages.

useCases.title: Cache Hit Ratio Trending
useCases.value: Cache hit ratio over 30 days reveals memory sizing issues, key churn, and upstream slowdowns that force more origin fetches. Declining trends often precede latency SLO breaches.

useCases.title: Message Queue Backlog Trending
useCases.value: Queue depth over 7 and 30 days shows sustained consumer lag versus transient spikes. Growth trends drive consumer scaling, partition adds, or poison-message handling before disk limits or SLA misses.

useCases.title: Brute-Force Login Detection
useCases.value: Brute-force attacks are a primary credential compromise vector. Early detection prevents account takeover.

useCases.title: Account Lockout Monitoring
useCases.value: Lockouts cause user productivity loss and help desk load. Source identification enables rapid resolution.

useCases.title: Privileged Group Membership Changes
useCases.value: Adding accounts to Domain Admins or Enterprise Admins (EventCode 4728/4732/4756) in minutes limits blast radius from stolen Tier-0 credentials. Immediate detection supports audit evidence for privileged access changes and enables rapid containment before lateral movement escalates.

useCases.title: Service Account Anomalies
useCases.value: Service accounts used interactively or from unexpected hosts indicate compromise. Detection prevents lateral movement.

useCases.title: Kerberos Ticket Anomalies
useCases.value: Detects Kerberoasting and Golden Ticket attacks, which are advanced AD compromise techniques. Essential for security monitoring.

useCases.title: Password Policy Violations
useCases.value: Failed password changes indicate users struggling with policy or potential social engineering. Monitoring supports security awareness.

useCases.title: GPO Modification Detection
useCases.value: GPO changes affect all domain-joined machines. Unauthorized modifications can disable security controls across the organization.

useCases.title: AD Replication Monitoring
useCases.value: Replication failures cause authentication issues, stale group memberships, and inconsistent policy application across sites.

useCases.title: LDAP Query Performance
useCases.value: Expensive LDAP queries degrade DC performance affecting authentication for all users. Detection enables query optimization.

useCases.title: Stale Account Detection
useCases.value: Stale accounts are an attack surface — unused accounts may be compromised without detection. Regular cleanup reduces risk.

useCases.title: Entra ID Risky Sign-Ins
useCases.value: Entra ID Identity Protection detects risky sign-ins using Microsoft's threat intelligence. Ingesting into Splunk enables correlation with on-prem events.

useCases.title: Conditional Access Policy Failures
useCases.value: Conditional Access blocks indicate non-compliant devices or policy misconfigurations. Monitoring ensures security policies work without excessive user friction.

useCases.title: AD Certificate Services Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Internal CA-issued certificates approaching expiry; missed renewals cause outages.

useCases.title: Service Account Password Age
useCases.value: Service accounts with passwords older than policy permits increase risk exposure.

useCases.title: Kerberoasting Detection
useCases.value: Attackers request weakly encrypted TGS tickets for service accounts to crack passwords offline. Focused Kerberoasting detection complements generic Kerberos monitoring.

useCases.title: Golden Ticket Indicators
useCases.value: Forged TGTs often produce anomalous ticket lifetimes, encryption types, or DC sourcing. Heuristic alerts support hunt teams when krbtgt may be compromised.

useCases.title: Entra Conditional Access Policy Changes
useCases.value: Policy edits can weaken MFA, device compliance, or location controls org-wide. Auditing changes supports SOC2/ISO and incident response.

useCases.title: Hybrid Join Device Compliance
useCases.value: Hybrid Azure AD join state and Intune compliance gate access; drift from compliant blocks users and signals stale or tampered endpoints.

useCases.title: LAPS Password Rotation Failures
useCases.value: Failed LAPS rotations leave predictable local admin passwords; attackers target stale LAPS attributes.

useCases.title: AD Replication Topology Changes
useCases.value: New connections, site link, or bridgehead changes can indicate persistence or misconfiguration affecting auth paths.

useCases.title: AdminSDHolder Modification
useCases.value: Changes to AdminSDHolder or SDProp timing can preserve attacker persistence on privileged accounts.

useCases.title: GPO Tampering Detection
useCases.value: Tampering via SYSVOL (file-level) may bypass 5136-only monitoring. File integrity on GPO paths catches unauthorized edits.

useCases.title: Entra PIM Activation Audit
useCases.value: Privileged Identity Management activations grant time-bound admin roles; auditing ensures approvals and detects abuse.

useCases.title: Stale Computer Account Cleanup
useCases.value: Stale computer objects enable rogue domain joins and clutter access reviews. Tracking supports automated disable/delete workflows.

useCases.title: AD Forest Trust Changes
useCases.value: Trust direction and selective authentication changes alter cross-forest attack surface; distinct from one-off session events.

useCases.title: Certificate Template Abuse (ESC Attacks)
useCases.value: Misconfigured templates (ESC1/ESC8) allow domain escalation via certificate requests. Monitoring issuance and template edits reduces exposure.

useCases.title: Active Directory Replication
useCases.value: AD replication failures cause authentication inconsistencies — users locked out in one site but not another, stale GPOs, and split-brain scenarios.

useCases.title: AD Certificate Services (ADCS) Anomalies
useCases.value: ADCS misconfigurations enable privilege escalation (ESC1-ESC8 attacks). Monitoring certificate requests catches unauthorized certificate enrollment for domain admin impersonation.

useCases.title: Bind Failure Monitoring
useCases.value: LDAP bind failures indicate authentication issues, misconfigured applications, or brute-force attempts against directory services.

useCases.title: Search Performance Degradation
useCases.value: Slow LDAP searches impact all applications relying on directory services for authentication and authorization.

useCases.title: Schema Modification Audit
useCases.value: Schema changes to directory services can break applications and are rarely expected. Detection ensures change control compliance.

useCases.title: Replication Health Monitoring
useCases.value: LDAP replication failures cause authentication inconsistencies and stale directory data across sites.

useCases.title: LDAP Query Volume Anomalies
useCases.value: Sudden spikes in LDAP searches may indicate reconnaissance, brute enumeration, or misbehaving applications hammering directory services.

useCases.title: Bind Failure Rate Spikes

useCases.title: Active Directory Schema Modification Audit

useCases.title: LDAP Signing Enforcement
useCases.value: Unsigned LDAP binds expose credentials to interception. Tracking enforcement and bind failures ensures GPO and domain controller settings are effective.

useCases.title: LDAPS Certificate Validation
useCases.value: LDAPS clients failing TLS handshakes or cert validation indicate expired CAs, hostname mismatches, or MITM attempts.

useCases.title: LDAP Channel Binding Status
useCases.value: Channel binding tokens for LDAP/SASL mitigate relay attacks; monitoring confirms clients meet `ldapEnforceChannelBinding` policy.

useCases.title: LDAP Referral Chaining Monitoring
useCases.value: Excessive or looping referrals degrade auth and may indicate misconfigured base DNs or cross-domain abuse.

useCases.title: MFA Challenge Failure Rate
useCases.value: High MFA failure rates indicate user friction, potential phishing, or MFA fatigue attacks. Monitoring supports both security and user experience.

useCases.title: Impossible Travel Detection
useCases.value: Authentication from two geographically distant locations within an impossibly short timeframe strongly indicates credential compromise.

useCases.title: Token Anomaly Detection
useCases.value: Token replay attacks bypass authentication entirely. Detection prevents persistent unauthorized access.

useCases.title: Application Access Patterns
useCases.value: Monitors which applications users access for license optimization and detects anomalous access indicating potential compromise.

useCases.title: IdP Availability Monitoring
useCases.value: IdP outage blocks all SSO authentication across the organization. Rapid detection enables failover and communication.

useCases.title: Phishing-Resistant MFA Adoption
useCases.value: Tracks migration from phishable factors (SMS, phone) to phishing-resistant factors (FIDO2, WebAuthn). Supports zero-trust maturity goals.

useCases.title: Session Hijacking Detection
useCases.value: Sessions used from multiple locations simultaneously indicate session token theft. Detection prevents ongoing unauthorized access.

useCases.title: SAML Assertion Replay Detection
useCases.value: Replayed SAML assertions can grant access without fresh authentication. Correlating assertion IDs and NotOnOrAfter windows catches reuse.

useCases.title: OAuth Token Abuse
useCases.value: Excessive refresh grants, scope expansion, or token use from new ASNs indicates stolen refresh tokens or malicious OAuth clients.

useCases.title: SSO Session Hijacking Indicators
useCases.value: Complements session ID correlation with user-agent flips, ASN changes mid-session, and impossible concurrent SSO from IdP telemetry.

useCases.title: Federated Trust Modifications
useCases.value: Adding SAML/OIDC federation to new domains or apps expands blast radius; auditing trust metadata changes is essential.

useCases.title: Consent Grant Abuse
useCases.value: Users granting excessive delegated permissions to malicious OAuth apps is a common attack; monitoring consent events enables revocation.

useCases.title: App Registration Secret Expiry
useCases.value: Expired client secrets break automation and encourage long-lived secrets; proactive alerting avoids outages and insecure workarounds.

useCases.title: Multi-Tenant App Access Anomalies
useCases.value: Unexpected tenants or guest users accessing multi-tenant apps may indicate consent phishing or lateral SaaS movement.

useCases.title: OAuth Scope Creep Detection
useCases.value: Applications accumulating scopes over time violate least privilege; comparing current vs approved scopes finds drift.

useCases.title: Token Endpoint Rate Limiting
useCases.value: Throttling at `/oauth2/token` breaks integrations and may indicate credential stuffing or runaway automation.

useCases.title: Privileged Session Audit
useCases.value: Complete audit trail of privileged sessions is required for compliance (SOX, PCI, HIPAA) and security investigation.

useCases.title: Password Checkout Tracking
useCases.value: Unusual checkout patterns may indicate misuse. Tracking ensures accountability and supports investigations.

useCases.title: Break-Glass Account Usage
useCases.value: Break-glass accounts provide emergency access and should rarely be used. Any usage requires immediate investigation and documentation.

useCases.title: Credential Rotation Compliance
useCases.value: Overdue password rotations increase exposure window if credentials are compromised. Compliance tracking ensures policy adherence.

useCases.title: Suspicious Session Commands
useCases.value: Detecting dangerous commands during privileged sessions enables real-time intervention before damage occurs.

useCases.title: Vault Health Monitoring
useCases.value: PAM vault downtime prevents all privileged access, blocking critical operations. Health monitoring ensures continuous availability.

useCases.title: Federated Identity Provider Health
useCases.value: IdP outages block all federated application access. Health monitoring ensures SSO availability and rapid incident response.

useCases.title: API Token Usage Anomaly
useCases.value: Unusual API token usage may indicate token theft or abuse. Detection supports least-privilege and incident response.

useCases.title: Cross-Domain Trust Change Detection
useCases.value: Trust relationship changes can enable cross-domain abuse. Early detection prevents privilege escalation across forests.

useCases.title: Just-in-Time Access Request Monitoring
useCases.value: JIT access reduces standing privilege. Monitoring request and approval patterns ensures policy compliance and detects abuse.

useCases.title: Identity Sync Failure Detection
useCases.value: Sync failures cause stale or missing identities in target systems, leading to access denials or orphaned accounts. Detection enables quick remediation.

useCases.title: RADIUS / TACACS+ Server Response Time
useCases.value: Authentication server latency and availability for network device auth; slow or unavailable RADIUS/TACACS+ blocks admin access to routers and switches.

useCases.title: Active Directory Domain Controller Response Time
useCases.value: LDAP bind time, DNS query time per DC — slow DCs cause auth delays and user lockouts.

useCases.title: CyberArk Session Recording Alerts
useCases.value: Real-time alerts on PSM recordings—policy violations, blocked commands, or session anomalies—enable SOC response before logout.

useCases.title: Privileged Session Duration Anomalies
useCases.value: Sessions far longer than peer baseline may indicate data exfiltration or abandoned hijacked sessions.

useCases.title: Vault Synchronization Failures
useCases.value: Vault replication or DR sync failures risk split-brain or stale credentials; distinct from generic component health.

useCases.title: Just-in-Time Access Request Analysis
useCases.value: Analytics on JIT volume, self-approval, and after-hours patterns complements simple volume alerts (UC-9.4.10).

useCases.title: Emergency Break-Glass Account Usage
useCases.value: Real-time paging for emergency-only vault accounts beyond standard break-glass (UC-9.4.3)—includes usage from non-SOC networks.

useCases.title: Shared Account Concurrent Login Detection
useCases.value: Shared privileged accounts used from two locations simultaneously indicate credential sharing or theft.

useCases.title: PAM Agent Health Monitoring
useCases.value: CPM, PSM, and PVWA agents offline block rotation and session capture; distinct from vault binary health (UC-9.4.6).

useCases.title: Okta Authentication Failures
useCases.value: Spikes in failed logins reveal credential attacks, misconfigured apps, or lockout conditions before accounts are fully compromised.

useCases.title: Okta MFA Bypass Attempts
useCases.value: Attempts to skip or weaken MFA (policy gaps, risky grant flows) are a direct path to account takeover; monitoring policy evaluation outcomes closes that gap.

useCases.title: Okta Suspicious Sign-In Activity
useCases.value: Okta threat signals and anomalous sessions (new device, new country, Tor) surface account takeovers before lateral movement.

useCases.title: Okta Admin Console Changes
useCases.value: Changes in the admin console affect global security posture; auditing who changed what supports SOC2/ISO investigations and insider-threat programs.

useCases.title: Okta Policy Modifications
useCases.value: Sign-on, MFA, and password policy edits can weaken security org-wide; detecting unauthorized or out-of-window changes is essential for governance.

useCases.title: Okta New Admin Creation
useCases.value: New super-admin or role assignments are high-value targets for attackers; immediate notification enables rapid validation.

useCases.title: Duo Authentication Denials
useCases.value: Denied logins (fraud, policy, or lockout) indicate attacks or misconfigurations; volume and user patterns guide response.

useCases.title: Duo Device Trust Posture
useCases.value: Non-compliant or out-of-date devices that still attempt access signal policy gaps and endpoint risk exposure.

useCases.title: Duo Enrollment Anomalies
useCases.value: Sudden bulk enrollments or enrollments from unusual locations can indicate attacker-driven device registration or help-desk abuse.

useCases.title: Federated SSO Token Abuse
useCases.value: Excessive OAuth/OIDC grants, refresh-token reuse, or token minting from new clients can indicate session theft or malicious automation.

useCases.title: Impossible Travel Detection (Okta)
useCases.value: Two successful sessions from geolocations that cannot be reached in the elapsed time indicate credential theft or shared accounts.

useCases.title: Okta API Rate Limit Monitoring
useCases.value: Hitting rate limits breaks automation, integrations, and provisioning; trending usage prevents surprise throttling during peak loads.

useCases.title: Okta App Assignment Changes
useCases.value: New access to sensitive SaaS apps is a common attack path; monitoring assignments supports least-privilege and access reviews.

useCases.title: Duo Push Fraud Detection
useCases.value: Push bombing and fraudulent approve taps are common MFA bypass techniques; correlating push volume and user behavior stops approval fatigue attacks.

useCases.title: Okta User Lifecycle Events (Provisioning / Deprovisioning)
useCases.value: Orphaned accounts, failed deprovisions, and unexpected creates drive audit findings and residual access after employee exit.

useCases.title: Device Compliance Status and Policy Enforcement
useCases.value: Ensures all managed devices comply with security policies and configuration standards.

useCases.title: Mobile Device Enrollment and MDM Status Tracking
useCases.value: Tracks device enrollment status to ensure mobile device management coverage.

useCases.title: Geofencing Alerts and Location-Based Policy Triggers
useCases.value: Uses geofencing to detect when devices leave secure zones and trigger location-based policies.

useCases.title: Mobile Security Policy Violations and App Restrictions
useCases.value: Detects policy violations and restricted app usage attempts.

useCases.title: Lost Mode Device Activation and Recovery Tracking
useCases.value: Tracks activation of lost mode on devices to ensure recovery protocols are working.

useCases.title: Mobile App Deployment Success Rate and Distribution Status
useCases.value: Tracks app deployment success and identifies devices with failed or incomplete deployments.

app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices)
useCases.title: Authentication Volume Trending
useCases.value: Daily authentication success and failure volumes show whether login load, credential attacks, or misconfiguration are drifting over a quarter. A seven-day moving average smooths weekly noise so you can spot sustained shifts before they overwhelm help desks or mask intrusions.

useCases.title: MFA Adoption Rate Trending
useCases.value: Tracking the percentage of users enrolled in multi-factor authentication over time proves progress toward zero-trust and regulatory expectations. Flat or declining adoption after rollout indicates gaps in onboarding, excluded groups, or integration problems that leave accounts easier to abuse.

useCases.title: Privileged Account Activity Trending
useCases.value: Privileged logon volume should be relatively stable; spikes can indicate credential theft, mass admin activity during an incident, or automation run amok. Trending over thirty days highlights gradual increases that point-in-time thresholds miss.

useCases.title: Service Account Usage Trending
useCases.value: Service accounts should authenticate in predictable volumes from known automation. A dormant account suddenly trending upward may indicate compromise, scope creep, or shadow IT scripts. Ninety-day views expose slow burns and seasonal batch jobs alike.

app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices)
useCases.title: Conditional Access Policy Block Trending
useCases.value: Tracking which conditional access policies block the most sign-ins over time shows whether controls are too strict, mis-targeted, or under attack. Policy-level trends support tuning reviews and prove enforcement for audits without relying on one-off investigations.

app: Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow or your ITSM (optional)
useCases.title: Password Reset Volume Trending
useCases.value: Sudden increases in password resets—self-service or helpdesk—often align with phishing waves, credential stuffing after a breach, or attacker-driven resets. A ninety-day trend with a moving average makes campaign-scale activity visible before individual tickets pile up.

app: vendor status is optional enrichment only
useCases.title: Identity Provider Availability Trending
useCases.value: Identity provider outages block all applications that rely on them; weekly or monthly uptime trends show whether your vendor or network path is degrading over a quarter. That supports SLA discussions, architecture decisions, and communication to the business before users flood the service desk.
