useCases.title: NERC CIP Physical Security Perimeter Log Review
useCases.value: Aligns with NERC CIP-006 by auditing physical access events to critical facilities housing BES cyber assets.

useCases.title: NERC CIP System Security Management Patch Tracking
useCases.value: Supports NERC CIP-007 by tracking patch status and timelines for BES Cyber Assets, reducing exploitable vulnerabilities on cyber systems.

useCases.title: NERC CIP Incident Reporting Timeline Compliance
useCases.value: Enforces NERC CIP-008 by verifying cyber incidents involving BES Cyber Systems are detected and escalated within required reporting timelines.

useCases.title: OT Network Baseline Deviation Detection
useCases.value: Detects new protocols, ports, or connections relative to learned OT baselines (T0840), highlighting shadow connectivity and preparatory attack activity.

useCases.title: User Peer-Group Logon Volume Anomaly (MLTK)
useCases.value: Comparing each user's authentication volume to their peer group (same department, role, or location) surfaces compromised accounts and insider threats that per-user baselines alone cannot catch — a user whose logon count is normal for themselves but triple the peer average is a strong anomaly signal.

useCases.title: Lateral Movement via Rare Destination Hosts (MLTK)
useCases.value: Attackers moving laterally connect to hosts they have never accessed before. By modeling each user's typical destination set and flagging first-seen or statistically rare destinations, this detection catches post-compromise pivoting that static ACLs and signature rules cannot see.

useCases.title: C2 Beaconing Detection via Time-Series Regularity (MLTK)
useCases.value: Command-and-control (C2) implants call home at regular intervals. By measuring inter-arrival time variance for each src-dest-port tuple, this detection identifies periodic beaconing that blends into normal traffic volumes — catching Cobalt Strike, Sliver, and custom implants that frequency-based rules miss.

useCases.title: Credential Stuffing Burst Detection vs Baseline (MLTK)
useCases.value: Credential stuffing attacks generate sudden spikes in failed authentication from distributed sources. By baselining normal failure rates per application endpoint and flagging statistical outliers, this detection catches automated credential replay before account lockouts cascade.

useCases.title: Risk Score Calibration with Supervised ML (MLTK)
useCases.value: Risk-Based Alerting assigns scores heuristically, but not all risk events are equal. Training a supervised model on analyst-confirmed true/false positives re-weights risk contributions so the aggregate score better predicts real incidents — reducing alert fatigue and focusing SOC attention on the highest-fidelity signals.

useCases.title: Phishing Email NLP Classification (DSDL)
useCases.value: Rule-based phishing filters miss novel lure themes and zero-day phishing kits. A pre-trained NLP classifier scores email subjects and body snippets for phishing intent — catching social engineering campaigns, BEC attempts, and spear-phishing that bypass gateway reputation checks.

useCases.title: Notable Event Prioritization Model (MLTK)
useCases.value: SOC analysts face hundreds of notables daily. A machine learning ranking model that predicts which notables are most likely true positives — based on historical disposition, asset criticality, risk score, time-of-day, and correlated events — lets the queue self-sort so analysts investigate the highest-value alerts first.

useCases.title: User and Entity Behavior Analytics — Anomalous Process Execution (MLTK)
useCases.value: Establishing per-host baselines of normal process execution and flagging rare or never-before-seen processes catches fileless malware, living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins), and novel toolkits that signature-based EDR misses.

useCases.title: Attack Surface Change Trending
useCases.value: Tracking newly exposed services and listening ports over time reveals shadow IT, misconfigurations, and scan gaps before attackers find them. Sudden increases in open ports or services often precede breaches or follow failed change control.

useCases.title: SIEM Alert-to-Incident Ratio Trending
useCases.value: Comparing ES notables to analyst-confirmed incidents shows whether the SOC is drowning in noise or under-escalating real cases. A falling ratio over 90 days may mean tuning drift; a rising ratio can indicate improved correlation or staffing effects worth validating.

useCases.title: Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) Trending
useCases.value: MTTD measures how quickly the organization notices malicious activity after it starts. Quarter-over-quarter trending supports leadership reporting, purple-team exercises, and investment in detection content versus response tooling.

useCases.title: Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) Trending
useCases.value: MTTR reflects containment and remediation speed once a detection exists. Sustained increases may signal playbook gaps, staffing shortages, or complex multi-domain incidents; decreases validate SOAR and runbook maturity.

useCases.title: Phishing Attempt Volume Trending
useCases.value: Weekly volume of blocked phishing attempts indicates campaign intensity and user targeting. Spikes justify awareness programs, mailbox rule reviews, and gateway tuning without waiting for a successful compromise.

app: Splunk App for Palo Alto Networks
useCases.title: Firewall Rule Hit Rate Trending
useCases.value: Top rules by hit count over 30 days expose noisy policies, overly broad permits, and candidates for segmentation review. Flat or rising hit rates on “catch-all” rules often precede policy hygiene projects.

useCases.title: Risk Score Distribution Trending
useCases.value: A shifting histogram of Enterprise Security risk scores shows whether the environment is accumulating unmanaged risk objects or whether tuning and closure activities are working. Persistent high-score tails warrant entity prioritization and threat-hunting focus.

useCases.title: Endpoint Protection Coverage Trending
useCases.value: Percentage of endpoints with current antivirus or EDR definitions and healthy agent status demonstrates control effectiveness for audits and cyber insurance. Downward trends often track OS rebuilds, mergers, or agent failures rather than policy alone.

useCases.title: Mail Flow Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Deferred or failed message traces directly hit revenue-dependent communications and support SLAs. Sustained delivery failure spikes should drive incident severity classification and trigger customer communication templates before users report the issue.

useCases.title: Mailbox Audit Logging
useCases.value: Tracks who accesses what mailboxes, including delegate and admin access. Essential for insider threat detection and compliance.

useCases.title: Exchange Online Protection Events
useCases.value: EOP filtering metrics show email threat landscape and security control effectiveness.

useCases.title: Teams Usage Analytics
useCases.value: Teams adoption and quality metrics inform collaboration strategy and help identify user experience issues.

useCases.title: SharePoint/OneDrive Sharing Audit
useCases.value: External sharing can expose sensitive data. Audit trail ensures data protection and compliance.

useCases.title: DLP Policy Events
useCases.value: M365 DLP policy matches across email, Teams, SharePoint identify sensitive data exposure. Centralized tracking supports compliance.

useCases.title: Admin Activity Audit
useCases.value: M365 admin actions (user creation, license changes, policy modifications) need audit trails for compliance and security.

useCases.title: Inbox Rule Monitoring
useCases.value: Malicious inbox rules (auto-forward to external, auto-delete) are a key post-compromise technique for data exfiltration.

app: Custom API input (M365 Service Health API)
useCases.title: Service Health Monitoring
useCases.value: M365 service incidents affect all users. Early awareness from API enables proactive communication and workaround planning.

useCases.title: License Utilization
useCases.value: M365 license costs are significant. Tracking utilization identifies unused licenses for reallocation and cost savings.

useCases.title: Exchange Message Queue Depth
useCases.value: Hub transport queue length indicates mail flow issues. Messages stuck in queue cause delivery delays, NDRs, and user complaints. Growing queues often precede transport service failures.

useCases.title: Exchange Database Copy Queue Length
useCases.value: DAG replication lag measured in number of log files. Growing copy queue risks data loss on failover and indicates replication or disk I/O issues. Replay queue lag affects failover time.

useCases.title: Admin Console Audit
useCases.value: Admin actions in Google Workspace affect all users. Audit trail supports compliance and detects unauthorized changes.

useCases.title: Gmail Message Flow
useCases.value: Email delivery monitoring and DLP enforcement protects sensitive data and ensures business communication reliability.

useCases.title: Drive Sharing Anomalies
useCases.value: Unusual file sharing patterns may indicate data exfiltration or accidental exposure of sensitive documents.

useCases.title: Login Anomaly Detection
useCases.value: Suspicious login activity (new device, unusual location, failed MFA) indicates potential account compromise.

useCases.title: Meet Quality Monitoring
useCases.value: Poor meeting quality impacts productivity and user satisfaction. Monitoring enables network/infrastructure optimization.

useCases.title: Third-Party App Access
useCases.value: OAuth app grants to third-party applications create data access risks. Monitoring enables governance and risk assessment.

useCases.title: Drive External Sharing Alerts
useCases.value: Alerts on files and folders shared outside the primary domain or with `anyone with link`—complements anomaly baselines (UC-11.2.3).

useCases.title: Admin Console Audit (Security Settings)
useCases.value: Focused on security-sensitive admin events (2SV, SSO, API keys)—extends general admin audit (UC-11.2.1).

useCases.title: Gmail Suspicious Forwarding
useCases.value: Detects auto-forwarding and delegation to external addresses—common post-compromise behavior.

useCases.title: Chrome Management Policy Compliance
useCases.value: Managed Chrome browsers should enforce updates, extensions allowlists, and safe browsing; drift indicates unmanaged or tampered clients.

useCases.title: Google Vault Hold Compliance
useCases.value: Hold creation, release, and matter changes affect legal preservation; errors risk spoliation findings.

useCases.title: Workspace Marketplace App Review
useCases.value: New marketplace app installs can expose Drive/Gmail data; tracks installs and OAuth scopes.

useCases.title: Groups Membership Changes
useCases.value: Sensitive Google Groups (all-staff, external partners) membership changes can broadly expose mail and Drive.

useCases.title: Cloud Identity Device Management
useCases.value: Endpoint visibility for mobile and desktop enrolled in Endpoint Verification / MDM—lost devices and OS drift.

useCases.title: Google Meet Quality Metrics
useCases.value: Meet quality telemetry (packet loss, jitter, RTT) for troubleshooting conferencing issues—extends UC-11.2.5 with org-level rollups.

useCases.title: Gmail Phishing Report Analysis
useCases.value: User-reported phishing provides ground-truth for tuning secure links and awareness; volume spikes indicate campaigns.

useCases.title: Workspace DLP Rule Violations
useCases.value: Google Workspace DLP incidents for Drive, Gmail, Chat—centralized for compliance trending.

useCases.title: Google Takeout Monitoring
useCases.value: Takeout requests export large user datasets—strong indicator of insider risk or compromised account.

useCases.title: Call Quality Monitoring — MOS (Cisco CUCM)
useCases.value: MOS scores directly measure voice quality experience. Degradation impacts business communication and customer service.

useCases.title: Call Volume Trending (Cisco CUCM)
useCases.value: Call volume patterns support capacity planning and detect anomalies (toll fraud, system issues).

useCases.title: VoIP Jitter/Latency/Packet Loss (Cisco CUCM)
useCases.value: Transport quality metrics identify network issues affecting voice quality before users report problems.

useCases.title: Trunk Utilization (Cisco CUCM)
useCases.value: Trunk capacity limits cause busy signals and missed calls. Monitoring prevents capacity-related service degradation.

useCases.title: Conference Bridge Capacity (Cisco CUCM)
useCases.value: Conference bridge resource exhaustion prevents users from joining meetings. Monitoring ensures adequate capacity.

useCases.title: Toll Fraud Detection (Cisco CUCM)
useCases.value: Toll fraud causes significant financial loss. International premium-rate calls from compromised systems can cost thousands per hour.

useCases.title: Phone Registration Status (Cisco CUCM)
useCases.value: Mass phone de-registration indicates network or UCM issues affecting the entire communications infrastructure.

useCases.title: Webex Meeting Analytics
useCases.value: Meeting analytics support collaboration optimization, license management, and quality improvement initiatives.

useCases.title: Mailbox Size and Quota Trending
useCases.value: Mailbox growth and quota usage help plan storage and avoid user lockouts. Trending supports capacity planning and proactive quota increases.

useCases.title: Email Forwarding Rule and Auto-Reply Audit
useCases.value: Unauthorized forwarding rules can exfiltrate mail; auto-replies may leak sensitive info. Auditing rule changes supports security and compliance.

useCases.title: Collaboration App Permission and Consent Audit
useCases.value: Third-party app consent and OAuth grants can expose data. Auditing consent and permission changes reduces shadow IT and abuse risk.

useCases.title: Voicemail and Call Recording Retention Compliance
useCases.value: Voicemail and call recordings may be subject to retention and deletion policies. Monitoring supports compliance and storage management.

useCases.title: Outbound Email Volume and Domain Anomaly
useCases.value: Spike in outbound volume or new recipient domains can indicate compromise or data exfiltration. Baseline comparison supports early detection.

app: Webex Meeting Qualities API (Pro Pack required)
useCases.title: Webex Meeting Quality Degradation Detection
useCases.value: Proactively detects poor meeting experiences by monitoring MOS scores, packet loss, jitter, and latency per participant. Enables IT to identify network segments, ISPs, or locations that consistently deliver degraded quality — before users start complaining. Supports SLA reporting and vendor accountability for Webex Calling and Meetings.

app: Webex Detailed Call History API (Pro Pack required)
useCases.title: Webex Calling CDR and Call Flow Analysis
useCases.value: Provides full call detail records for Webex Calling, enabling cost analysis, trunk utilization tracking, call flow optimization, and identification of failed or abandoned calls. Unlike on-premise UCM CDRs, this covers cloud-native Webex Calling deployments. Supports chargebacks, capacity planning, and troubleshooting call routing issues through auto-attendants and call queues.

useCases.title: Webex Calling Queue Performance and SLA
useCases.value: Monitors call queue health metrics that directly impact customer experience: average wait time, abandon rate, SLA compliance, and agent availability. Enables real-time staffing decisions and long-term workforce planning. High abandon rates or long wait times indicate understaffing or routing problems that need immediate attention.

useCases.title: Webex Admin Audit Trail
useCases.value: Provides full accountability for administrative changes in Webex Control Hub — user provisioning, policy changes, license assignments, security settings, and integration modifications. Required for compliance audits (SOX, HIPAA, ISO 27001) and security investigations. Detects unauthorized admin actions or compromised admin accounts through anomaly detection on change volume and timing.

useCases.title: Webex DLP and File Compliance Monitoring
useCases.value: Monitors real-time file sharing across Webex spaces for data loss prevention violations. Files are scanned before becoming accessible to other members, preventing sensitive data exposure. Tracks DLP approval/rejection decisions, identifies repeat offenders, and provides evidence for compliance investigations. Critical for organizations handling PII, PHI, financial data, or intellectual property in Webex.

useCases.title: Webex Device Health and Environmental Monitoring
useCases.value: Monitors the health and environmental conditions of Webex room devices (Room Kit, Board, Desk series). RoomOS devices report temperature, humidity, ambient noise, air quality, and occupancy data via RoomAnalytics. Detecting devices that go offline, run outdated firmware, or operate in poor environmental conditions prevents meeting disruptions and protects hardware investments. Occupancy data from room sensors supports real estate optimization.

useCases.title: Webex License Utilization and Adoption Tracking
useCases.value: Compares assigned Webex licenses against actual usage to identify wasted spend. Organizations often over-provision Meetings, Calling, and Messaging licenses. Tracking adoption rates by department and user helps right-size license allocations, reclaim unused seats, and justify renewals. Combines license inventory data with meeting/calling activity to calculate true utilization rates.

useCases.title: Webex Messaging Activity and Anomaly Detection
useCases.value: Tracks messaging volume, file sharing, and space activity across Webex Messaging. Establishes baselines per user to detect anomalous bulk messaging that could indicate a compromised account, bot abuse, or policy violation. Also measures collaboration adoption and engagement trends across departments. Identifies inactive spaces consuming storage and active spaces that may need governance controls.

useCases.title: SharePoint Site Storage Utilization
useCases.value: Site collections approaching quota block uploads and disrupt teams. Proactive monitoring enables quota increases or content archival before users hit limits.

useCases.title: SharePoint Search Crawl Health
useCases.value: Crawl errors, stale content, and index freshness affect findability. Failed crawls leave content undiscoverable; slow crawls delay new content visibility.

useCases.title: SIP Server Availability Monitoring (ThousandEyes)
useCases.value: Monitors SIP server reachability from ThousandEyes agents, ensuring voice and unified communications infrastructure is responsive from the network path perspective. SIP server failures directly impact call setup for all users.

useCases.title: SIP Registration Time Tracking (ThousandEyes)
useCases.value: Slow SIP registration or response times indicate server overload, network congestion, or infrastructure issues that delay call setup and affect voice quality perception.

useCases.title: RTP MOS Score Monitoring (ThousandEyes)
useCases.value: Mean Opinion Score (MOS) is the standard measure of voice call quality on a scale of 1 to 5. ThousandEyes RTP tests provide MOS alongside packet loss, discards, and delay variation, enabling continuous voice quality assurance from the network perspective.

useCases.title: Webex Meeting Quality Assurance via ThousandEyes
useCases.value: Monitors the network path from offices to Webex data centers using ThousandEyes agents, providing proactive visibility into network conditions that degrade meeting quality — before users file tickets. Correlate with Webex quality data (UC-11.3.6) for end-to-end troubleshooting.

useCases.title: Microsoft Teams Network Readiness (ThousandEyes)
useCases.value: Validates that each office location meets Microsoft's network quality requirements for Teams calls and meetings (latency <50ms, loss <1%, jitter <30ms). ThousandEyes tests the actual network path to Microsoft 365 endpoints.

useCases.title: Zoom Collaboration Performance (ThousandEyes)
useCases.value: Monitors network path quality to Zoom data centers from office locations, ensuring the network supports high-quality video conferencing. Helps distinguish between Zoom platform issues and local network problems.

useCases.title: RoomOS Device Network Health via ThousandEyes
useCases.value: ThousandEyes agents can be enabled on Cisco RoomOS devices (Room Kit, Board, Desk), monitoring the network path from the conference room to cloud meeting services. This provides per-room visibility into network conditions affecting meeting quality.

useCases.title: Wire-Level VoIP Quality (MOS from RTP Stream)
useCases.value: Captures Mean Opinion Score (MOS) and R-Factor directly from RTP packets on the wire, providing platform-independent voice quality measurement. Unlike UC-11.3.1 which uses Cisco CUCM CMR data (application-level), this use case captures quality at the network level regardless of the call platform — covering third-party PBX, SIP trunking providers, and carrier interconnects.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: Emergency Call (E911/E112) Tracking
useCases.value: Tracks all emergency calls (911, 933 test, 112) through the telephony system to ensure regulatory compliance and rapid response. Monitors call completion rate, answer time, and any failed emergency calls — a regulatory requirement in many jurisdictions.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: Answer Seizure Ratio (ASR) by Route Group
useCases.value: Calculates Answer Seizure Ratio — the percentage of call attempts that are successfully answered — by route group or trunk. ASR is the primary KPI for voice service quality in carrier networks. Low ASR indicates trunk failures, destination unreachable, or capacity exhaustion.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: CUCM CDR Call Path Analysis
useCases.value: End-to-end call routing visibility across gateways, trunks, route patterns, and route lists exposes misconfigured route plans that silently send calls through unintended paths — causing unexpected PSTN charges, degraded codec quality, or failed calls that users report as "the phone just doesn't work." CDR path analysis turns cryptic cause codes into actionable routing intelligence.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: CUCM CMR Call Quality Heatmap
useCases.value: Beyond per-call MOS monitoring (UC-11.3.1), mapping CMR metrics — MOS, jitter, concealed seconds, severely concealed seconds, latency — by site-pair reveals which network segments consistently degrade voice quality. A site-to-site heatmap transforms thousands of individual call quality records into an instant visual that network engineers can use to prioritize WAN/SD-WAN optimization.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: CUCM Phone Firmware Compliance
useCases.value: IP phone firmware versions determine security posture and feature availability. Phones running end-of-support firmware are vulnerable to known exploits and may lack critical features like encrypted RTP. Tracking firmware across a fleet of thousands of phones via CUCM syslog registration events provides automated compliance reporting that replaces manual CUCM Admin page audits.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: CUCM Gateway and CUBE Utilization
useCases.value: PSTN gateways and CUBE (Cisco Unified Border Element) have finite channel capacity. When all channels are in use during peak hours, additional calls receive busy signals or route to overflow destinations that may incur higher PSTN costs. Monitoring channel utilization against capacity prevents revenue-impacting call failures and supports trunk procurement decisions.

useCases.title: CUCM Cluster Database Replication Health
useCases.value: CUCM relies on Informix database replication between publisher and subscriber nodes to synchronize configuration and runtime data. Replication failures cause configuration drift — changes made on the publisher don't propagate, causing inconsistent dial plans, missing device registrations, and failover failures. Detecting replication lag or broken replication before it impacts call processing prevents hard-to-diagnose intermittent call failures.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: CUCM Call Admission Control (CAC) Rejection Trending
useCases.value: Call Admission Control prevents WAN link saturation by rejecting calls when bandwidth allocation is exhausted for a location pair. CAC rejections mean users hear reorder tone or get rerouted to PSTN (higher cost). Trending CAC rejections by location directly supports SD-WAN, MPLS, and QoS capacity planning by quantifying where and when voice bandwidth demand exceeds allocation.

app: TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics (Splunkbase #4434)
useCases.title: CUCM Hunt Group and Line Group Overflow
useCases.value: Hunt pilots distribute incoming calls across line groups (e.g., helpdesk, sales, reception). When all members of a line group are busy, calls overflow to the next group or voicemail. Excessive overflow indicates understaffing, misconfigured hunt lists, or members not logging into their phones. Tracking overflow rates per hunt pilot directly supports workforce management and ensures callers reach a live agent rather than voicemail during business hours.

useCases.title: Webex Contact Center Agent State and Occupancy
useCases.value: Agent state distribution directly determines customer wait times and contact center throughput. Agents stuck in "Not Ready" or spending excessive time in "Wrap-Up" reduce effective capacity without appearing as staffing shortages. Real-time and trended agent state analytics expose hidden productivity issues, validate workforce management schedules, and provide evidence for staffing adjustments that reduce customer wait times.

useCases.title: Webex Contact Center IVR Containment Rate
useCases.value: IVR containment rate measures the percentage of callers who complete their task within the IVR self-service system without speaking to a live agent. High containment reduces agent workload and cost per contact. Declining containment signals IVR menu confusion, new customer issues not covered by self-service, or technical failures in IVR integrations (database lookup failures, speech recognition errors) — all of which increase agent queue volume and customer frustration.

useCases.title: Webex Contact Center Customer Wait Time SLA by Skill Group
useCases.value: Queue-level SLA metrics hide performance disparities across skill groups. A blended 80% service level may mask that billing support hits 95% while technical support languishes at 55%. Granular skill-group SLA tracking exposes which specializations need staffing adjustments, schedule optimization, or skills-based routing tuning — directly preventing customer churn in the skill groups that matter most to revenue.

useCases.title: UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring
useCases.value: Cisco Unified Contact Center Express (UCCX) remains widely deployed for small-to-medium contact centers. Native UCCX reporting is limited to historical views, and Finesse supervisor gadgets show only a single queue at a time. Splunk aggregation of UCCX queue statistics provides a unified real-time and historical view across all Contact Service Queues (CSQs), enabling supervisors to spot developing queue emergencies and workforce planners to validate staffing models with actual data.

useCases.title: Contact Center Abandon Rate Correlation with Network Quality
useCases.value: Contact center abandons have two fundamentally different root causes: callers hanging up because of long wait times (staffing issue) vs callers disconnected due to network/voice quality failures (infrastructure issue). Distinguishing these requires correlating abandon events with network quality metrics. Misdiagnosing network-caused abandons as staffing issues wastes workforce budget; misdiagnosing wait-time abandons as network issues wastes engineering effort.

useCases.title: Jabber Client Version Compliance and Health
useCases.value: Cisco Jabber clients run on Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android with different version lifecycles and vulnerability profiles. Outdated Jabber versions may have known security vulnerabilities (CVEs), lack support for current SRTP/TLS standards, or miss critical bug fixes. Fleet-wide version tracking replaces manual inventory audits and supports security compliance reporting by quantifying the attack surface from legacy communication clients.

useCases.title: IM and Presence Service Availability
useCases.value: Cisco IM and Presence (IM&P) provides XMPP-based instant messaging, presence status, and federation with external systems. IM&P node failures cause presence to show all users as "Unknown," messages to queue indefinitely, and inter-cluster federation to break. Unlike voice call failures which produce immediate user complaints, IM&P degradation often goes unreported for hours while quietly impacting team coordination and collaboration workflows.

useCases.title: Unity Connection Voicemail System Health
useCases.value: Cisco Unity Connection handles voicemail, auto-attendant, and Interactive Voice Response functions. Port exhaustion during peak hours causes callers to hear busy signals instead of reaching voicemail. Message store capacity issues cause new messages to be rejected. MWI (Message Waiting Indicator) delivery failures leave users unaware of waiting messages. Monitoring these components prevents the silent voicemail failures that users only discover when someone says "didn't you get my message?"

useCases.title: Unity Connection Mailbox Usage and Retention Compliance
useCases.value: Voicemail mailboxes that grow unbounded consume storage and may violate data retention policies (PCI, HIPAA, legal hold requirements). Users who never check voicemail accumulate messages that represent both a storage cost and a compliance risk. Tracking mailbox sizes, message aging, and auto-deletion policy compliance ensures the voicemail system operates within governance boundaries and storage capacity is allocated to active users rather than abandoned mailboxes.

useCases.title: Pexip Conference Volume and Concurrency Trending
useCases.value: Pexip Infinity clusters have finite conferencing node capacity. Understanding conference volume patterns — peak hours, concurrent participant counts, and growth trends — is essential for capacity planning and license procurement. Unexpected spikes can exhaust node resources, causing new conferences to fail or existing ones to degrade. Tracking concurrency against licensed capacity prevents brownouts during company all-hands or large training events.

useCases.title: Pexip Participant Call Quality Monitoring
useCases.value: Pexip calculates call quality based on packet loss: Good (<1%), OK (<3%), Bad (<10%), Terrible (>=10%). Unlike platforms that only report aggregate quality, Pexip media stream statistics provide per-participant, per-stream metrics including jitter and packet loss for both audio and video. Identifying quality degradation by participant, location, or protocol allows targeted remediation — a site with consistently bad quality likely has a WAN problem, while a single participant with issues may have a local network or endpoint problem.

useCases.title: Pexip Conferencing Node Capacity and Load
useCases.value: Pexip Conferencing Nodes process all media transcoding and conference hosting. Each node has a finite capacity measured in HD call equivalents. When a node reaches capacity, new calls are either routed to other nodes (if available) or rejected. Uneven load distribution across nodes wastes capacity — one overloaded node may reject calls while others sit idle. Monitoring per-node load ensures efficient resource usage and prevents capacity-related call failures.

useCases.title: Pexip License Consumption Tracking
useCases.value: Pexip licensing is typically based on concurrent ports or participants. Exceeding licensed capacity prevents new participants from joining conferences. Under-utilization means wasted license spend. Tracking actual consumption against purchased licenses supports renewal negotiations with real data, identifies peak usage patterns for right-sizing, and provides early warning when growth trends approach license limits.

useCases.title: Pexip Alarm and Service Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Pexip Infinity generates alarms for infrastructure problems: database connectivity loss, licensing errors, node unreachability, certificate expiry, and media resource exhaustion. These alarms represent active service risks that can escalate to conference failures. Centralizing alarm monitoring in Splunk provides correlation with other infrastructure events and enables faster incident response than checking the Pexip management console manually.

useCases.title: Pexip Registration and Gateway Call Routing
useCases.value: Pexip acts as a gateway between different video conferencing protocols and platforms — SIP, H.323, WebRTC, and Microsoft Teams via the Teams Connector. Call routing rules determine how incoming calls reach their destination VMR (Virtual Meeting Room) or are forwarded to external systems. Routing failures cause participants to reach wrong destinations or fail to connect entirely. Monitoring registration status and gateway routing ensures interoperability between the Pexip infrastructure and external systems like CUCM, Teams, or third-party SIP endpoints.

useCases.title: Pexip Participant Join Failure Analysis
useCases.value: When participants fail to join a Pexip conference, the disconnect reason reveals the root cause: capacity exhaustion, authentication failure, codec mismatch, network timeout, or policy rejection. Understanding the distribution and trend of join failures by reason enables targeted remediation. A spike in "capacity" failures means nodes need scaling; "codec mismatch" failures mean endpoint configuration needs updating; "timeout" failures point to network problems between participant and conferencing node.

useCases.title: Pexip Interoperability and Protocol Mix
useCases.value: Pexip's core value proposition is interoperability — connecting participants across SIP, H.323, WebRTC, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Understanding the protocol mix reveals how the platform is actually being used versus its intended deployment. A shift from H.323 to WebRTC signals endpoint modernization. Growing Teams Connector traffic validates the hybrid meeting room investment. Protocol distribution also affects capacity planning because different protocols consume different amounts of transcoding resources on Conferencing Nodes.

useCases.title: SMTP Service Availability
useCases.value: Distinct from mail queue depth monitoring — this checks whether the SMTP daemon is accepting TCP connections and responding to EHLO. A crashed postfix or sendmail process stops inbound/outbound mail entirely without generating queue entries. Nagios `check_smtp` verifies this at the connection layer; Splunk replicates it via daemon-level log monitoring.

useCases.title: POP3 / IMAP Mail Retrieval Service Availability
useCases.value: POP3 and IMAP services allow mail clients to retrieve messages. Even when delivery works correctly, a crashed Dovecot or Cyrus daemon prevents users from reading email, appearing as a total mail outage. Nagios `check_pop` and `check_imap` monitor these ports directly; Splunk replicates availability detection through daemon log analysis.

useCases.title: Mail Queue Depth and Deferred Message Backlog
useCases.value: Growing mail queue (deferred, hold) indicates delivery failures, recipient issues, or abuse. Detecting backlog early prevents bounce storms and blacklisting.

useCases.title: SMTP Authentication and Relay Policy Violations
useCases.value: Failed SMTP auth or unauthorized relay attempts may indicate credential stuffing or abuse. Monitoring supports security and ensures relay policy is enforced.

useCases.title: Mail Delivery Rate and Bounce Rate by Domain
useCases.value: Sudden drop in delivery rate or spike in bounces for a domain indicates reputation or configuration issues. Trending supports deliverability and capacity planning.

useCases.title: Outbound Mail Volume and Recipient Anomaly
useCases.value: Unusual outbound volume or new bulk recipients may indicate compromised account or phishing campaign. Baseline and anomaly detection support incident response.

useCases.title: Mail Server TLS and Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Expired or expiring TLS certificates on SMTP/IMAP/POP break encryption and can cause delivery failures. Proactive monitoring prevents outages.

useCases.title: SMTP Relay Monitoring
useCases.value: Tracks messages relayed through internal SMTP gateways vs policy — unexpected relay volume or open relay abuse paths.

useCases.title: Zoom Meeting Quality Metrics (Jitter, Packet Loss, Latency)
useCases.value: Poor jitter, loss, or latency directly degrades audio/video MOS and drives support tickets; trending these metrics isolates client, ISP, or Zoom POP issues before executive calls fail.

useCases.title: Zoom Call Drop Rate Monitoring
useCases.value: Elevated drop rates signal network instability, client bugs, or capacity limits; tracking drops by geography and client version prioritizes fixes.

useCases.title: Zoom Participant Join Failures
useCases.value: Join failures block users from hearings and classes; clustering failures by error code reveals SSO, licensing, or capacity misconfigurations.

useCases.title: Webex Device Health
useCases.value: Room devices with high CPU, thermal, or firmware errors degrade meetings; proactive health reduces onsite truck rolls and VIP room incidents.

useCases.title: Webex Room System Uptime
useCases.value: Room system availability underpins executive and boardroom SLAs; uptime trending supports hardware refresh and network path decisions.

useCases.title: Video Conferencing License Utilization
useCases.value: Underused licenses waste budget; near-capacity entitlements risk meeting blocks during peaks—utilization guides true-up and consolidation across Zoom/Webex/Teams.

useCases.title: Meeting Recording Storage Trending
useCases.value: Cloud recording storage grows with retention policies; trending consumption avoids surprise overages and informs lifecycle rules for compliance vs. cost.

app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services
useCases.title: Teams Meeting Quality Analysis
useCases.value: Teams Call Quality Dashboard (CQD) data exposes poor Wi‑Fi, VPN, or PSTN legs; Splunk rollups unify CQD with org context for targeted network fixes.

useCases.title: Meeting Room No-Show and Early Release Trending
useCases.value: Meeting rooms are expensive corporate assets. Rooms booked but never occupied (no-shows) and meetings that end well before the booked time waste capacity that other teams need. Quantifying no-show rates and early release patterns provides facilities and IT leadership with evidence to implement auto-release policies, shorten default booking durations, and right-size room inventory — directly improving room availability without adding physical space.

useCases.title: Meeting Room People Count vs Capacity Optimization
useCases.value: A 20-person boardroom consistently used by 2-person meetings represents a massive space efficiency failure. Conversely, 4-person huddle rooms packed with 8 people violate fire codes and degrade meeting quality. RoomOS people count data matched against room capacity enables evidence-based space optimization — converting underutilized large rooms into multiple smaller spaces, or adding capacity where demand exceeds supply — decisions worth millions in real estate savings.

useCases.title: Meeting Room AV Equipment Health
useCases.value: "The screen doesn't work" is the most common meeting room complaint. By monitoring display/projector power state, camera connectivity, microphone mute state at meeting start, speaker health, and peripheral connectivity via RoomOS xAPI status events, IT can detect and fix equipment failures before users encounter them. Proactive AV monitoring transforms reactive room support into preventive maintenance, reducing meeting disruptions and executive frustration.

useCases.title: Digital Signage and Room Scheduler Device Health
useCases.value: Webex-powered digital signage displays and room schedulers (Room Navigator panels mounted outside meeting rooms) are visible indicators of IT reliability. A blank Room Navigator outside a boardroom or a frozen digital signage screen in the lobby creates a poor impression for visitors and employees. Monitoring these devices for connectivity, content delivery, and responsiveness prevents embarrassing failures in high-visibility locations.

useCases.title: Commit Activity Trending
useCases.value: Commit velocity indicates team productivity and project health. Drops may signal blockers; spikes may precede release issues.

useCases.title: Branch Protection Bypasses
useCases.value: Direct pushes to protected branches bypass code review, introducing unreviewed code to production. Detection ensures process compliance.

useCases.title: Pull Request Metrics
useCases.value: PR cycle time affects development velocity. Long review times indicate bottlenecks; abandoned PRs indicate scope or alignment issues.

useCases.title: Secret Exposure Detection
useCases.value: Secrets committed to source control are immediately compromised. Detection within minutes enables rapid rotation before exploitation.

useCases.title: Repository Access Audit
useCases.value: Repository permission changes can expose source code to unauthorized users. Audit trail supports IP protection and compliance.

useCases.title: Force Push Detection
useCases.value: Force pushes overwrite git history, potentially destroying code and audit trails. Detection ensures accountability.

useCases.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Run Time Trending
useCases.value: Workflow duration growth over time indicates growing tech debt, resource constraints, or inefficient pipeline design. Early detection enables optimization before velocity degrades.

useCases.title: GitHub Actions Billing Usage
useCases.value: Approaching included minutes quota risks unexpected overages or workflow throttling. Proactive monitoring prevents billing surprises and supports capacity planning.

useCases.title: Branch Protection Bypass Detection
useCases.value: Complements UC-12.1.2 by correlating audit `protected_branch.policy_override` with push events for investigation packs.

useCases.title: Force Push to Protected Branches
useCases.value: Narrows UC-12.1.6 to default/release branches where history rewrite has highest impact.

useCases.title: Sensitive File Commit Detection
useCases.value: Paths such as `.env`, `id_rsa`, `kubeconfig`, and `*.pem` in commits indicate credential sprawl even before secret scanning fires.

useCases.title: Repository Permission Changes
useCases.value: Team `maintain`/`admin` grants and visibility changes to `public` are higher risk than member adds (UC-12.1.5).

useCases.title: PR Review Bypass Detection
useCases.value: Merges with zero approvals or with only self-approval violate four-eyes policies.

useCases.title: Fork Network Suspicious Activity
useCases.value: Sudden stars/forks from new accounts or geo clusters can precede supply-chain attacks or leaked-token cloning.

useCases.title: CODEOWNERS File Modification Monitoring
useCases.value: Attackers may weaken review requirements by editing `CODEOWNERS` or `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

useCases.title: Large File Commit Detection
useCases.value: Large blobs bloat repos, bypass review in diff viewers, and may hide embedded data.

useCases.title: Signed Commit Enforcement
useCases.value: Unsigned commits on protected branches weaken non-repudiation; verify GPG/SSH sig status.

useCases.title: Stale Branch Cleanup Tracking
useCases.value: Long-lived branches accumulate merge debt and stale code; tracking supports automated deletion policies.

useCases.title: Repository Webhook Health
useCases.value: Failed webhook deliveries break CI, security scanning, and Splunk ingestion—monitor delivery logs and HTTP status.

useCases.title: Code Scanning Alert Trends
useCases.value: GitHub Advanced Security CodeQL/code scanning alert open/close rates show remediation velocity and new debt.

useCases.title: Build Success Rate Trending
useCases.value: Declining build success rates indicate code quality issues, flaky tests, or infrastructure problems. Trending drives improvement.

useCases.title: Build Duration Monitoring
useCases.value: Increasing build times slow development velocity. Detection enables build optimization and infrastructure right-sizing.

useCases.title: Deployment Frequency (DORA)
useCases.value: Deployment frequency is a key DORA metric indicating engineering capability maturity. Higher frequency correlates with better outcomes.

useCases.title: Lead Time for Changes (DORA)
useCases.value: Lead time measures the commit-to-production pipeline efficiency. Shorter lead times enable faster value delivery and incident response.

useCases.title: Failed Deployment Tracking
useCases.value: Failed deployments cause service disruption. Rapid detection enables rollback decisions. Change failure rate is a DORA metric.

useCases.title: Pipeline Queue Time
useCases.value: Long queue times indicate insufficient CI/CD runner capacity, slowing developer feedback loops and delivery velocity.

useCases.title: Test Coverage Trending
useCases.value: Declining test coverage increases risk of undetected bugs. Trending ensures quality standards are maintained.

useCases.title: Security Scan Results in Pipeline
useCases.value: SAST/DAST/SCA findings in CI/CD pipelines catch vulnerabilities before they reach production. Tracking ensures security gates work.

useCases.title: Jenkins Executor Utilization
useCases.value: Busy executors as % of total and queue wait time indicate CI capacity. High utilization with long queue times signals need for additional agents or executor scaling.

useCases.title: Jenkins Node Offline Detection
useCases.value: Build agents going offline impacts CI capacity and causes job failures. Rapid detection enables agent recovery or failover before queue backlog grows.

useCases.title: GitLab CI Runner Availability
useCases.value: Runner registration status and job queue time affect CI throughput. Offline or paused runners cause jobs to wait or fail; monitoring ensures runner fleet health.

useCases.title: GitLab Pipeline Duration Trending
useCases.value: Pipeline getting slower over time indicates growing tech debt or resource constraints. Trending enables proactive optimization before developer velocity degrades.

useCases.title: Jenkins Agent Offline Alerts
useCases.value: Operational paging when executors disappear—complements UC-12.2.10 with severity tiers and agent labels (prod vs dev).

useCases.title: Pipeline Stage Duration Regression
useCases.value: Stage-level regression (e.g., `test` stage) surfaces before overall job duration crosses SLA (UC-12.2.2).

useCases.title: Build Artifact Integrity Verification
useCases.value: Compares published artifact checksums/Sigstore signatures against CI-recorded values to detect tampering at rest.

useCases.title: Deploy Approval Bypass Detection
useCases.value: Production deploys without change ticket or approval group in CD system (Spinnaker, Argo Rollouts, Harness).

useCases.title: Parallel Build Resource Contention
useCases.value: Runner saturation lengthens CI pipelines and causes flaky tests that block releases. Correlating saturation metrics with P95 job duration justifies autoscaling investment and prevents false 'code regression' blame when infrastructure is the root cause.

useCases.title: Flaky Test Detection
useCases.value: Tests that pass/fail without code changes waste time and hide real failures; quarantine candidates identified by pass rate variance.

useCases.title: Deployment Frequency Tracking
useCases.value: DORA dashboard slice—deployments per service per day with team and application tags (extends UC-12.2.3).

useCases.title: Lead Time for Changes (Percentile)
useCases.value: p95 lead time exposes tail latency hiding in averages (UC-12.2.4).

useCases.title: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
useCases.value: Time from incident detection or deploy failure to successful restore—core DORA metric.

useCases.title: Change Failure Rate
useCases.value: Ratio of failed deployments or hotfix-required releases to total deployments—DORA metric.

useCases.title: Pipeline Secret Rotation Compliance
useCases.value: CI/CD credentials (vault tokens, cloud API keys) approaching expiry without rotation break builds and create risk.

useCases.title: Build Queue Wait Time SLA
useCases.value: SLA-focused view of queue delay—% of jobs waiting >5 min (extends UC-12.2.6).

useCases.title: Test Coverage Regression
useCases.value: PRs that reduce line coverage vs main branch—visibility for governance (pair with CI gates).

useCases.title: Pipeline Resource Utilization
useCases.value: CPU/memory per runner job—right-sizing and spot vs on-demand mix.

useCases.title: Artifact Repository Health
useCases.value: Full artifact repositories prevent builds from publishing. Storage monitoring and cleanup policy verification ensures CI/CD continuity.

useCases.title: Dependency Vulnerability Alerts
useCases.value: Vulnerable dependencies in the software supply chain are a primary attack vector. Tracking ensures timely patching.

useCases.title: Package Download Anomalies
useCases.value: Unusual package download patterns may indicate dependency confusion attacks or compromised internal packages.

useCases.title: License Compliance Tracking
useCases.value: Open-source license violations create legal risk. Automated tracking ensures compliance before code reaches production.

useCases.title: Terraform State Drift Detection
useCases.value: Planned vs. applied resource count and drift between declared and actual infrastructure indicate manual changes or state corruption. Detection ensures IaC remains source of truth and supports compliance audits.

useCases.title: Container Image Vulnerability Scan Failures
useCases.value: CI gate failures when Trivy/Grype/ECR scanning cannot pull image or scanner errors—distinct from found CVEs (UC-12.3.2).

useCases.title: Package Dependency Audit Alerts
useCases.value: New AGPL/GPL or typosquat package names in lockfiles—policy engine output beyond CVE severity.

useCases.title: Artifact Retention Policy Compliance
useCases.value: Verifies cleanup jobs deleted snapshots per policy; stale artifacts past retention indicate failed garbage collection.

useCases.title: SBOM Generation Compliance
useCases.value: CycloneDX/SPDX missing for release builds breaks supply-chain attestation requirements (EO 14028).

useCases.title: Artifact Signing Verification
useCases.value: Cosign/Notary verification results at deploy time—signature missing or wrong key.

useCases.title: Package Provenance Tracking
useCases.value: SLSA provenance predicate links artifact digest to git source SHA and builder ID—detects builds not from trusted pipelines.

useCases.title: Registry Storage Growth
useCases.value: Daily growth rate of container/NPM registry—forecast disk exhaustion (extends UC-12.3.1).

useCases.title: Terraform Plan/Apply Tracking
useCases.value: Every Terraform apply changes infrastructure. Full audit trail enables change management, impact analysis, and rollback decisions.

useCases.title: Configuration Drift Detection
useCases.value: Drift from declared IaC state indicates manual changes that bypass change control, creating inconsistency and security risks.

useCases.title: Ansible Playbook Outcomes
useCases.value: Tracking Ansible run results ensures configuration management is working. Failed tasks indicate systems in unknown state.

useCases.title: Puppet/Chef Compliance Reports
useCases.value: Configuration management compliance ensures systems match desired state. Non-compliance indicates security or operational risk.

useCases.title: IaC Policy Violations
useCases.value: Policy-as-code (OPA/Sentinel) prevents non-compliant infrastructure from being provisioned. Tracking blocked deployments validates governance.

useCases.title: Pipeline Failure Root Cause Trending
useCases.value: Recurring failure causes (e.g., flaky tests, env issues) slow delivery. Trending root causes supports targeted remediation and stability.

useCases.title: Container Image Build and Push Audit
useCases.value: Unauthorized or untagged image pushes can introduce risk. Auditing build and push events supports supply chain security and compliance.

useCases.title: Release Gate and Approval Lag
useCases.value: Long approval or gate wait times delay releases. Monitoring gate duration and approval latency supports process improvement.

useCases.title: Feature Flag and Experiment Rollout Monitoring
useCases.value: Feature flags and experiments affect user experience. Monitoring rollout percentage and error rate per flag supports safe rollouts and rollback.

useCases.title: Deployment Rollback and Canary Health
useCases.value: Failed canaries or automatic rollbacks indicate bad releases. Tracking rollback rate and canary metrics ensures safe deployments.

useCases.title: ArgoCD Application Sync Status
useCases.value: Out-of-sync or degraded applications in ArgoCD indicate GitOps drift or deployment failures. Detection ensures desired state matches cluster state and enables rapid remediation.

useCases.title: Terraform Plan Drift Detection
useCases.value: Scheduled CI `terraform plan` runs that show changes when no pipeline apply occurred—focused operational view vs UC-12.4.2.

useCases.title: CloudFormation Stack Drift
useCases.value: AWS `DetectStackDrift` results show live resources diverging from template—essential for CloudFormation-centric teams.

useCases.title: Ansible Playbook Failure Tracking
useCases.value: Failure rate per playbook and run—trending layer on top of UC-12.4.3 outcomes.

useCases.title: Policy-as-Code Violation Trending
useCases.value: OPA, Sentinel, or Conftest denials over time—spikes after new policy rollout (extends UC-12.4.5).

useCases.title: IaC Module Version Compliance
useCases.value: Terraform module sources below approved minimum semver—reduces stale or vulnerable module usage.

useCases.title: ArgoCD Sync Status Failures
useCases.value: Failed or stuck sync operations leave clusters diverging from Git and block releases; surfacing them quickly limits blast radius and restores desired state.

useCases.title: ArgoCD Drift Detection
useCases.value: Live cluster drift from Git-defined manifests risks untracked changes and audit gaps; detecting drift prioritizes reconciliation before incidents or compliance findings.

useCases.title: Flux Reconciliation Health
useCases.value: Unhealthy Flux `Kustomization`/`HelmRelease` resources stop automated delivery; monitoring reconciliation ensures continuous GitOps and catches controller or source errors early.

useCases.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Failure Rate
useCases.value: A rising workflow failure rate signals flaky pipelines, bad merges, or infra issues that slow delivery and can block production paths.

app: GitHub Enterprise Server / self-hosted runner scripts
