useCases.value: Deep job queues delay CI feedback and releases; tracking queue depth distinguishes runner capacity problems from workflow volume spikes.

useCases.title: GitLab CI Pipeline Duration Regression
useCases.value: Sudden pipeline duration increases waste compute budgets and slow merges; regression detection isolates stages, runners, or dependencies that changed.

useCases.title: Deployment Rollback Frequency Tracking
useCases.value: Frequent rollbacks indicate release quality or progressive-delivery issues; tracking frequency supports blameless review and release process tuning.

useCases.title: Helm Release Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Failed or pending Helm releases leave workloads partially updated or broken; monitoring release status prevents silent partial deploys.

useCases.title: Kustomize Build Error Tracking
useCases.value: Kustomize build failures block manifests from applying; early detection shortens fix time for overlay, patch, or base reference mistakes.

useCases.title: GitOps Deployment Lead Time
useCases.value: Measuring Git commit-to-production lead time exposes bottlenecks in review, CI, and sync so teams can optimize end-to-end delivery speed.

app: optional Splunk DORA or custom summary searches
useCases.title: DORA Metrics Trending Dashboard
useCases.value: Deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, and restore time summarize delivery health; month-over-month trends show whether engineering investments actually improved flow or reliability.

useCases.title: Security Scan Finding Trending
useCases.value: Seeing new, open, and closed findings per sprint proves whether shift-left scanning and remediation keep pace with development; spikes in new findings after dependency upgrades are expected—flat open counts are not.

useCases.title: Build Queue Wait Time Trending
useCases.value: Queue wait reflects runner capacity and pipeline fan-in; rising waits delay feedback and release trains even when job success rates look fine.

useCases.title: Container Image Build Time Trending
useCases.value: Longer image builds slow every downstream deploy; sprint-level trends catch Dockerfile regressions, bloated layers, or registry latency before they dominate CI budgets.

useCases.title: Indexer Queue Fill Ratio
useCases.value: Backed-up indexing queues cause data loss or delay. Detection enables immediate investigation of ingestion bottlenecks.

useCases.title: Search Concurrency Monitoring
useCases.value: Exceeding search concurrency limits causes search skipping and degraded user experience. Monitoring guides capacity decisions.

useCases.title: Forwarder Connectivity
useCases.value: Silent forwarder failures mean data gaps that may not be noticed until an investigation fails. Detection ensures data completeness.

useCases.title: License Usage Trending
useCases.value: License overages cause enforcement (search blocking). Trending enables proactive management and capacity planning.

useCases.title: Skipped Search Detection
useCases.value: Skipped searches mean scheduled reports, alerts, and data enrichments aren't running. This creates blind spots in monitoring and compliance.

useCases.title: Index Size Trending
useCases.value: Index size growth affects storage costs and search performance. Trending enables proactive storage planning.

useCases.title: KV Store Health
useCases.value: KV Store failures break lookups, app functionality, and ES correlation. Health monitoring prevents cascading application issues.

useCases.title: Deployment Server Status
useCases.value: Deployment server issues prevent app/config distribution to forwarders, leaving them with stale or incorrect configurations.

useCases.title: Data Ingestion Latency
useCases.value: High indexing latency (difference between event time and index time) means stale data for searches. Detection enables root cause analysis.

useCases.title: Search Head Cluster Status
useCases.value: SHC member failures affect user access and search capacity. Captain election issues can cause complete SHC outage.

useCases.title: Indexer Cluster Bucket Replication
useCases.value: Under-replicated buckets mean data is at risk of loss. Monitoring ensures the replication factor is maintained.

useCases.title: HEC Endpoint Health
useCases.value: HEC is a primary data ingestion path. Failures silently drop data from applications, containers, and cloud services.

useCases.title: Sourcetype Breakdown Trending
useCases.value: Understanding data volume per sourcetype enables cost optimization, retention tuning, and unexpected growth detection.

useCases.title: Long-Running Search Detection
useCases.value: Long-running searches consume shared resources and may indicate poorly written SPL or excessive time ranges.

useCases.title: Splunk Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Expired Splunk internal certificates break inter-component communication (forwarder→indexer, SHC replication, etc.).

useCases.title: Parsing Queue Health (_internal)
useCases.value: A saturated parsing queue delays ingestion and increases `_indextime` lag. Tracking fill ratio and blocked state isolates pipeline bottlenecks before data loss.

useCases.title: Merging Queue Health (_internal)
useCases.value: Merging queue backlog delays structured indexing and can block hot buckets. Monitoring prevents silent pipeline stall on heavy merge workloads.

useCases.title: Typing Queue Health (_internal)
useCases.value: The typing queue applies rules to parsed events; backlog here delays field extraction and routing to indexes.

useCases.title: TCP Output Connection Failures (_internal)
useCases.value: Forwarders and intermediate tiers rely on TCP out to indexers. Connection failures mean data is queued or dropped at the source.

useCases.title: Modular Input Errors (_internal)
useCases.value: Scripted and modular inputs drive critical ingestion; errors stop or corrupt data collection without obvious UI failure.

useCases.title: Data Model Acceleration Status (_internal)
useCases.value: Failed or lagging accelerations break pivot searches, ES views, and app dashboards that depend on `tstats`.

useCases.title: Summary Indexing Failures (_internal)
useCases.value: Summary index population jobs feed exec and compliance reports; silent failures skew metrics and dashboards.

useCases.title: Indexer Disk Space Utilization (_internal)
useCases.value: Full indexer volumes stop writes and break replication; proactive disk monitoring avoids cascading cluster failure.

useCases.title: SmartStore Cache Hit/Miss Ratio (_internal)
useCases.value: Low cache hit rates increase S3/API latency and search cost. Trending hit/miss guides cache sizing and bucket locality.

useCases.title: Cluster Bundle Push Failures (_internal)
useCases.value: Failed bundle distribution leaves indexers with stale `indexes.conf`, apps, or peer configs, causing search/replication skew.

useCases.title: splunkd Unexpected Restart Detection (_internal)
useCases.value: Unplanned `splunkd` restarts interrupt searches, replication, and ingestion. Correlating restarts speeds root cause (OOM, crash, admin).

useCases.title: Splunk Web UI Errors (_internal)
useCases.value: Web UI 5xx/timeout errors block analysts during incidents. Tracking errors isolates SHC vs load balancer vs app issues.

useCases.title: SHC Configuration Replication Lag (_internal)
useCases.value: Lagging conf replication causes inconsistent searches and failed lookups across members.

useCases.title: Ingest Actions Pipeline Status (_internal)
useCases.value: Ingest actions (routing, filtering, streaming) failures drop or misroute security and operational data.

useCases.title: Timestamp Parsing Accuracy (_internal)
useCases.value: Mis-parsed timestamps break RT searches, compliance, and `_indextime` lag metrics.

useCases.title: Workload Management Pool Saturation (_internal)
useCases.value: WLM pools prevent search starvation; saturation delays critical searches and alerts.

useCases.title: Search Scheduler Fill Ratio (_internal)
useCases.value: Scheduler at capacity skips searches—blind spots for alerts and summaries.

useCases.title: Knowledge Bundle Size Monitoring (_internal)
useCases.value: Oversized knowledge bundles slow search distribution and SHC replication.

useCases.title: Real-Time Search Resource Consumption (_internal)
useCases.value: Real-time searches reserve cores and memory; runaway RT jobs degrade interactive and scheduled workload.

useCases.title: User Search Activity Audit (_audit)
useCases.value: Auditing who ran which searches supports insider-threat investigations and segregation of duties.

useCases.title: Configuration File Change Tracking (_audit)
useCases.value: Unauthorized `.conf` edits change data access and ingestion behavior; rapid detection limits blast radius.

useCases.title: Knowledge Object Modification Audit (_audit)
useCases.value: Dashboard and alert tampering can hide attacks or exfiltration; object-level audit supports SOC and GRC.

useCases.title: REST API Access Pattern Analysis (_audit)
useCases.value: Automated token abuse and reconnaissance often appear as unusual REST paths or volumes.

useCases.title: Role and Capability Change Detection (_audit)
useCases.value: Privilege escalation via new roles/capabilities must be detected in minutes, not days.

useCases.title: Per-Process CPU and Memory Trending (_introspection)
useCases.value: `splunkd` child processes (search, indexer, pipeline) resource trends predict OOM and slowdown before user impact.

useCases.title: Dispatch Directory Size (_introspection)
useCases.value: Large dispatch directories fill disk and slow search teardown—common after runaway searches or stuck jobs.

useCases.title: I/O Wait Bottleneck Detection (_introspection)
useCases.value: High I/O wait on indexers correlates with slow searches, bucket replication, and ingestion lag.

useCases.title: Splunk Version Compliance (operational inventory)
useCases.value: Drift across Splunk Enterprise versions breaks feature parity and support eligibility.

useCases.title: App Version Consistency Across SHC (operational inventory)
useCases.value: Mixed app versions on SHC members cause bundle skew and intermittent UI or search errors.

useCases.title: Forwarder Version Compliance (operational inventory)
useCases.value: Old universal forwarders miss TLS fixes and acknowledgment behaviors required by security policy.

useCases.title: Log Volume and Error Rate Anomaly per Sourcetype (MLTK)
useCases.value: Silent data pipeline breaks — a forwarder stops sending, a sourcetype drops to zero, or error rates spike — are invisible to threshold alerts that only fire on presence. By modeling expected log volume and error rate per sourcetype with MLTK, this detection catches ingestion failures within minutes instead of hours, preventing blind spots in security and operational monitoring.

useCases.title: License Usage Forecast with Seasonality (MLTK)
useCases.value: Splunk license overages trigger warnings and eventually block indexing. Forecasting daily license consumption with seasonal decomposition (weekly and monthly patterns) gives administrators 7–30 day advance warning to act — whether by reducing noisy sourcetypes, requesting license expansion, or shifting workloads.

useCases.title: Splunk Internal Queue Depth Multivariate Anomaly (MLTK)
useCases.value: Individual queue metrics (parsing, merging, typing, indexing) may fluctuate normally, but simultaneous pressure across multiple queues indicates a systemic bottleneck. Multivariate anomaly detection catches correlated queue saturation that per-queue thresholds miss, enabling proactive capacity intervention before data loss occurs.

useCases.title: Service Latency Seasonality and Anomaly (MLTK)
useCases.value: Application response times follow predictable patterns — higher during business hours, lower at night. By decomposing latency into seasonal (hour-of-week) and residual components, this detection flags abnormal slowdowns that coincide with deployments, infrastructure changes, or emerging incidents — even when raw latency stays within static thresholds.

useCases.title: Kubernetes HPA Replica Count Anomaly (MLTK)
useCases.value: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) replica counts reflect traffic load. Unexpected spikes in replicas without corresponding traffic increases may indicate resource leaks, crash loops, or misconfigured scaling policies. Anomaly detection on replica counts relative to traffic volume catches autoscaler misbehavior before it exhausts cluster capacity.

useCases.title: SLO Burn-Rate Multivariate Anomaly (MLTK)
useCases.value: Single-dimensional SLO burn-rate alerts trigger too late or too often. By combining error budget burn rates across availability, latency, and throughput SLOs into a multivariate model, this detection identifies services heading for SLO breach across multiple dimensions simultaneously — a stronger signal than any individual budget alarm.

useCases.title: Service Health Score Trending
useCases.value: Service health scores provide a single-pane view of business service status. Trending enables SLA reporting and proactive management.

useCases.title: KPI Degradation Alerting
useCases.value: KPI threshold breaches provide early warning of service degradation. Adaptive thresholds reduce false positives vs static thresholds.

useCases.title: Episode Volume and MTTR
useCases.value: Episode volume and resolution time measure IT operations effectiveness. Trending drives process improvement.

useCases.title: Entity Status Monitoring
useCases.value: Entity health provides granular visibility into individual infrastructure components feeding services. Unstable entities degrade service health.

useCases.title: Base Search Performance
useCases.value: ITSI base searches feed all KPIs. Slow or skipped base searches cause stale or missing KPI data across multiple services.

useCases.title: Rules Engine Health
useCases.value: The ITSI Rules Engine processes events into episodes. Failure means alerts are not grouped or routed, breaking Event Analytics.

useCases.title: Predictive Service Degradation
useCases.value: Predicting service health degradation before it happens enables proactive remediation, reducing incident impact.

useCases.title: Glass Table NOC Display
useCases.value: Real-time service visualization for operations centers provides at-a-glance awareness of infrastructure and service health.

useCases.title: Elasticsearch Ingest Pipeline Errors
useCases.value: Log pipeline processing failures causing data loss or corruption.

useCases.title: Fluentd / Fluent Bit Buffer Overflow
useCases.value: Log forwarding buffer full, data at risk of being dropped.

useCases.title: KPI Threshold Violation Trending
useCases.value: Trending KPI breaches over time shows chronic vs transient service issues and validates threshold tuning.

useCases.title: Episode Correlation Accuracy
useCases.value: Measuring false merges and missed splits improves aggregation policies and reduces analyst rework.

useCases.title: Maintenance Window Compliance
useCases.value: Incorrect maintenance flags hide real outages during change windows, while noisy KPI alerts during true maintenance erode analyst trust. This use case validates that ITSI `is_service_in_maintenance` flags align with ITSM change windows, catching both missing and stale flags.

useCases.title: Glass Table SLA Breaches
useCases.value: Glass Tables for NOC must reflect SLA-backed KPIs; breaches on the wallboard drive incident prioritization.

useCases.title: Service Dependency Health Propagation
useCases.value: Upstream dependency failure should roll up to dependent services; missing links cause wrong prioritization.

useCases.title: ITSI Backup Set Integrity
useCases.value: Corrupt or incomplete KV Store / ITSI backup objects prevent disaster recovery after SH loss.

useCases.title: Notable Event Suppression Audit
useCases.value: Over-suppression hides incidents; audit ensures suppress rules and analyst actions are justified.

useCases.title: Adaptive Thresholding Effectiveness
useCases.value: Adaptive thresholds reduce false positives; tracking effectiveness shows when to retrain or fall back to static limits.

useCases.title: Multi-Tier Application Service Tree Modeling
useCases.value: Service trees link infrastructure KPIs to business outcomes, enabling impact analysis that shows which component failure affects which customer-facing service.

useCases.title: Entity Discovery Completeness Audit
useCases.value: Undiscovered entities create monitoring blind spots. Auditing entity coverage against infrastructure inventories ensures every critical asset is monitored by ITSI services.

useCases.title: Content Pack Deployment Health (Monitoring and Alerting)
useCases.value: The Monitoring and Alerting content pack provides pre-built correlation searches and aggregation policies. Tracking deployment health ensures these critical components remain functional.

useCases.title: Notable Event Volume Trending by Source
useCases.value: Tracking notable event volume by source correlation search identifies noisy rules, misconfigured thresholds, and alert fatigue risks before they overwhelm analysts.

useCases.title: KPI Drift Detection for Gradual Degradation
useCases.value: Drift detection identifies gradual KPI value changes (e.g., slow memory leak, increasing latency) that stay within thresholds but indicate an emerging problem. Catches issues before threshold breach.

useCases.title: MLTK Custom Anomaly Detection on KPI Data
useCases.value: Combining MLTK with ITSI KPI data enables custom anomaly models that detect multi-dimensional patterns (e.g., CPU+memory+latency correlation) impossible with single-KPI thresholds.

useCases.title: Splunk On-Call (VictorOps) Alert Routing
useCases.value: Routing ITSI episode alerts to Splunk On-Call ensures the right on-call engineer is paged with full service context, reducing MTTA by eliminating manual triage.

useCases.title: Observability Cloud Alert Ingestion
useCases.value: Ingesting Splunk Observability Cloud alerts into ITSI unifies cloud-native and on-prem monitoring into a single episode management workflow, eliminating tool-switching.

useCases.title: Service Template Adoption and Consistency
useCases.value: Service templates ensure consistent KPI definitions, thresholds, and entity rules across environments (dev/staging/prod). Tracking adoption prevents configuration drift.

useCases.title: Entity-Level Adaptive Threshold Tuning
useCases.value: Entity-level adaptive thresholds (ITSI 4.20+) provide per-host baselines instead of aggregate, drastically reducing false positives in heterogeneous environments where host behavior varies.

useCases.title: Configuration Assistant Recommendations Tracking
useCases.value: The Configuration Assistant (ITSI 4.20+) provides AI-powered optimization recommendations. Tracking which recommendations are implemented vs ignored ensures continuous ITSI health improvement.

useCases.title: Deep Dive Utilization and Performance
useCases.value: Deep Dives are ITSI's primary investigation tool. Tracking utilization reveals which KPIs analysts actually use for troubleshooting and identifies slow-rendering dives that need optimization.

useCases.title: ITSI Team Permission and RBAC Audit
useCases.value: ITSI team assignments control service visibility and episode access. Auditing permissions ensures least-privilege access and prevents unauthorized service modifications.

useCases.title: Business Service SLA Composite Scoring
useCases.value: Composite SLA scores aggregate ITSI health data across services to produce contractual SLA metrics (e.g., 99.9% availability), directly supporting customer and executive reporting.

useCases.title: Episode MTTR Analysis by Service Tier
useCases.value: Breaking MTTR down by service tier (Tier 1 critical, Tier 2 important, Tier 3 internal) reveals whether high-priority services get faster resolution and identifies process bottlenecks.

useCases.title: ITSI License and Capacity Utilization
useCases.value: ITSI licensing is based on entity count and KPI volume. Tracking utilization prevents license overages and supports capacity planning for service expansion.

useCases.title: Azure Log Analytics Workspace Ingestion Health
useCases.value: Azure Log Analytics Workspace is the central logging destination for Azure Monitor, Defender for Cloud, and Sentinel. Ingestion lag or data cap throttling silently breaks alerting and investigation workflows across the entire Azure monitoring stack.

useCases.title: Entity-Level Multivariate Anomaly Detection (MLTK + ITSI)
useCases.value: ITSI's adaptive thresholds evaluate KPIs individually per service. But many real incidents manifest as subtle, simultaneous deviations across multiple KPIs for a single entity — CPU slightly elevated, memory climbing, response time drifting up. Per-entity multivariate anomaly detection via MLTK catches these correlated degradation patterns before any single KPI breaches its threshold, providing minutes of early warning for cascading failures.

useCases.title: Causal KPI Ranking — Root-Cause Acceleration (MLTK + ITSI)
useCases.value: When a parent service health score drops, operators must manually investigate child KPIs to find the root cause. A trained model that ranks which child KPIs best explain parent health changes accelerates root-cause analysis from minutes to seconds — showing "memory pressure on the database tier explains 68% of the service degradation" instead of requiring manual drill-down through dozens of KPIs.

useCases.title: Nagios/Zabbix Alert Ingestion
useCases.value: Consolidating legacy monitoring alerts into Splunk enables cross-tool correlation and single-pane-of-glass operations.

useCases.title: Prometheus Metric Ingestion
useCases.value: Ingesting Prometheus metrics into Splunk enables long-term storage, cross-domain correlation, and unified dashboarding.

useCases.title: PagerDuty/Opsgenie Integration
useCases.value: Tracking alert lifecycle and on-call response metrics ensures incident response SLAs are met and identifies process improvements.

useCases.title: Monitoring Coverage Gap Detection
useCases.value: Hosts not covered by any monitoring tool are blind spots. Detection ensures comprehensive infrastructure visibility.

useCases.title: Alert Storm Detection
useCases.value: Correlated alert storms across monitoring tools indicate major incidents. Detection enables rapid escalation and noise reduction.

useCases.title: SLO Burn Rate and Error Budget Tracking
useCases.value: Burn rate and error budget show how fast SLO is consumed. Tracking supports proactive action before SLA breach and prioritization of reliability work.

useCases.title: Distributed Trace Sampling and Coverage
useCases.value: Trace sampling rate and coverage affect observability. Monitoring sampling decisions and trace completeness supports tuning and gap detection.

useCases.title: Log Ingestion Backlog and Lag
useCases.value: Ingestion backlog or lag causes delayed alerting and search. Monitoring lag per source ensures data freshness and pipeline health.

useCases.title: Dashboard and Saved Search Usage Analytics
useCases.value: Usage of dashboards and saved searches guides optimization and retirement. Analytics support adoption and reduce stale or unused content.

useCases.title: Synthetic Check Failure and Geographic Variance
useCases.value: Synthetic checks validate user-facing availability. Failure or variance by geography highlights regional issues and CDN/edge health.

useCases.title: Prometheus Target Scrape Failures
useCases.value: Targets down or unreachable; gaps in metrics collection.

useCases.title: Prometheus TSDB Compaction Failures
useCases.value: Storage engine issues impacting metric retention.

useCases.title: Grafana Datasource Health
useCases.value: Datasource connectivity and query errors; broken dashboards.

useCases.title: OpenTelemetry Collector Dropped Spans and Metrics
useCases.value: Collector queue pressure causing data loss.

useCases.title: OpenTelemetry Collector Pipeline Throughput and Backpressure
useCases.value: The OTel Collector is a single point of failure for observability data. When exporters can't keep up with receiver intake, the batch processor queue fills and backpressure propagates upstream — first dropping low-priority data, then refusing new data entirely. By the time you notice missing traces in your backend, thousands of spans are already lost. Monitoring pipeline throughput and queue saturation in real-time catches backpressure within minutes, before it becomes data loss.

useCases.title: OpenTelemetry Collector Memory and CPU Utilization
useCases.value: OTel Collectors are Go processes that can OOM-kill under sustained load or memory leaks, especially with processors like `groupbytrace` or `tail_sampling` that hold data in memory. A killed collector creates a gap in observability data exactly when you need it most — during incidents. Tracking heap allocation growth patterns and CPU utilization catches runaway collectors before the OOM killer does.

useCases.title: OpenTelemetry Collector Configuration Drift Detection
useCases.value: In a fleet of dozens or hundreds of OTel Collector instances (DaemonSets, gateway deployments, agent sidecars), configuration inconsistency causes silent observability failures. One collector running a stale config may be missing a processor, dropping a signal type, or exporting to a decommissioned endpoint — while appearing healthy. Configuration drift detection ensures every collector runs the intended config after rollouts, preventing partial observability gaps.

useCases.title: OpenTelemetry Receiver Health by Signal Type
useCases.value: Each OTel Collector receiver (OTLP, Jaeger, Prometheus, filelog, hostmetrics) independently accepts or refuses data by signal type (traces, metrics, logs). A receiver that starts refusing spans while accepting metrics indicates endpoint-specific authentication failures, protocol mismatches, or resource exhaustion on a single pipeline. Per-receiver, per-signal health monitoring pinpoints exactly which instrumentation endpoint is broken, reducing MTTR from "something is wrong with observability" to "the Jaeger receiver on collector-5 is refusing spans due to gRPC auth errors."

useCases.title: OpenTelemetry Exporter Retry and Timeout Monitoring
useCases.value: OTel Collector exporters retry failed sends with exponential backoff. Persistent retry failures indicate backend unavailability, authentication expiry, or network partitions. Timeouts indicate backend performance degradation that slows the entire pipeline. Monitoring retry counts and timeout rates per exporter and destination prevents the cascade where a slow backend fills queues, triggers backpressure, and ultimately causes data loss across all signals — not just the one with the failing backend.

useCases.title: LLM API Latency and Error Rate (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI)
useCases.value: High latency or error rates on managed LLM endpoints directly impact user experience and SLOs; tracking both by model and region isolates provider issues versus client misuse.

useCases.title: Token Usage and Cost per Model and Application
useCases.value: Token spend ties directly to budget and chargeback; per-application and per-model views prevent surprise bills and highlight inefficient prompts or runaway automation.

useCases.title: GPU and TPU Utilization for Inference Workloads
useCases.value: Underutilized accelerators waste capex; saturated GPUs increase queue time and latency for inference—utilization guides autoscaling and instance right-sizing.

useCases.title: Model Version Deployment Tracking
useCases.value: Knowing which model revision serves production supports rollback, audit, and safety reviews when behavior or cost shifts after a rollout.

useCases.title: AI Gateway Rate Limiting and Quota Management
useCases.value: Gateway limits protect backends and budgets; monitoring 429s and quota headers prevents one client from starving others and validates limit tuning.

app: ESCU (Analytic Story: Local LLM abuse patterns)
useCases.title: Ollama Local LLM Abuse Detection (ESCU)
useCases.value: Self-hosted Ollama endpoints can be probed or misused for bulk generation; correlating ESCU-style analytics with local logs catches abuse before resource exhaustion or data leakage.

useCases.title: MCP Server Suspicious Activity Detection (ESCU)
useCases.value: Model Context Protocol servers expose tools and data to agents; anomalous tool invocation or auth patterns may indicate compromise or prompt-driven misuse.

useCases.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Data Exfiltration Risk (ESCU)
useCases.value: Copilot can surface sensitive content; monitoring risky prompts and large exports supports insider-threat and DLP alignment with Microsoft’s recommended logging.

useCases.title: LLM Prompt Injection Attempt Detection
useCases.value: Injection attempts try to override system instructions or exfiltrate context; logging and alerting limits abuse before secrets or policies are bypassed.

useCases.title: AI Model API Key Rotation Compliance
useCases.value: Stale API keys increase breach impact; proving rotation cadence supports security policy and vendor audits.

useCases.title: LLM Output Content Policy Violation Logging
useCases.value: Provider and organizational safety filters block harmful content; logging violations supports red-teaming, policy tuning, and audit trails for regulated use cases.

useCases.title: AI Inference Pipeline Error Rate
useCases.value: End-to-end inference includes preprocess, model call, and postprocess; pipeline-level error rates catch failures that raw HTTP 200s miss (e.g., empty generations, schema errors).

useCases.title: Seq2Seq Log Anomaly Detection via Reconstruction Error (DSDL)
useCases.value: Traditional log monitoring relies on known patterns — regex, keywords, error codes. But novel failures, zero-day exploits, and subtle misconfigurations produce log lines that have never been seen before. An LSTM or Transformer autoencoder trained on normal log sequences learns the "grammar" of healthy log output and flags lines with high reconstruction error — catching anomalies that no predefined rule could anticipate.

useCases.title: Host-Metric Heatmap Anomaly via CNN (DSDL)
useCases.value: Infrastructure metrics (CPU, memory, disk I/O, network throughput) per host form a time × metric matrix that looks like an image. A Convolutional Neural Network trained on these "metric heatmaps" detects complex, multi-metric degradation patterns — such as the specific combination of rising CPU, flat memory, and oscillating disk I/O that precedes a particular failure mode — that univariate thresholds and even multivariate statistical models cannot capture.

useCases.title: MLTK Model Drift and Performance Monitoring
useCases.value: All ML models deployed in production (security detections, capacity forecasts, anomaly detectors) degrade as data distributions shift. Without drift monitoring, a model that was 95% accurate at deployment may silently drop to 60% accuracy over months. This meta-use-case tracks model health metrics so teams know when to retrain before detection quality degrades.

useCases.title: Trace Duration Anomaly and Slow Transaction Detection
useCases.value: A deployment that adds 200ms to a critical checkout flow costs revenue every second it runs. Static latency thresholds generate noise during normal traffic variation and miss gradual regressions. By baselining p50/p95/p99 trace duration per service and operation, this detection identifies statistically significant latency regressions within minutes of a deployment — before enough users complain to reach support.

useCases.title: Trace Error Rate by Service and Operation
useCases.value: Error rate is the most immediate signal of service degradation. Tracking error spans (status_code=ERROR) by service, operation, and error type creates accountability: each team sees their service's error contribution. When the checkout service suddenly jumps from 0.1% to 5% errors on the `processPayment` operation, the payment team gets alerted immediately rather than waiting for downstream impact to cascade.

useCases.title: Trace Completeness and Orphan Span Detection
useCases.value: Incomplete traces — missing parent spans, single-span traces from multi-service flows, or orphaned spans with no root — indicate broken context propagation, missing instrumentation, or sampling inconsistencies. These gaps make distributed debugging impossible exactly when it matters most. Measuring trace completeness quantifies instrumentation quality and identifies which services need propagation fixes.

useCases.title: Cross-Service Dependency Map from Traces
useCases.value: Service-to-service dependencies are often undocumented, especially in microservice architectures where teams add new API calls without updating architecture diagrams. Auto-discovering the dependency graph from trace data reveals the actual topology — including unexpected edges that represent security risks (why is the frontend calling the billing database directly?) or change risks (this "isolated" service actually has 12 downstream dependents). New edges appearing after deployments are an immediate change management signal.

app: any log framework with OTel integration
useCases.title: Log-to-Trace Correlation Coverage
useCases.value: Logs without trace context are isolated events that can't be correlated to specific user requests. When only 30% of log events carry `trace_id` and `span_id`, debugging a failed request requires manual timestamp-based guesswork across services. Measuring log-trace correlation coverage per service quantifies instrumentation maturity and identifies which teams need to add OTel context propagation to their logging frameworks.

useCases.title: Trace Fanout and Depth Anomaly
useCases.value: Traces with unusually high span counts or deep nesting reveal N+1 query patterns, recursive service calls, and runaway microservice chains that consume disproportionate resources. A single API call generating 10,000 spans indicates a loop or unbounded fan-out that impacts both application performance and observability infrastructure cost. Detecting these "mega-traces" prevents both performance degradation and observability platform overload.

app: Splunk Add-on for Splunk Observability Cloud
useCases.title: Splunk APM Service Map Health (RED Metrics)
useCases.value: Splunk APM's service map provides real-time Request rate, Error rate, and Duration (RED) metrics per service and endpoint. Ingesting these metrics into Splunk Enterprise enables correlation with infrastructure data, security events, and business metrics that live outside Observability Cloud — creating a unified view that neither platform provides alone. Degrading RED metrics in APM can trigger Splunk Enterprise workflows, populate ITSI service trees, or enrich ES risk scores.

useCases.title: Splunk APM Database Query Performance
useCases.value: Database spans in APM traces reveal which SQL queries contribute most to service latency. A single unoptimized query hiding behind 50ms average response time can drive p99 to 2 seconds. APM database query analysis identifies the specific queries and calling services responsible for database-driven latency, providing actionable evidence for query optimization and index tuning — bridging the gap between application and database teams.

useCases.title: Splunk RUM Core Web Vitals Tracking
useCases.value: Google's Core Web Vitals — Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) — directly impact search ranking and user experience. Splunk RUM captures these metrics per page, browser, device type, and geographic location. Tracking CWV trends detects regressions after frontend deployments before they affect SEO ranking or user conversion rates. A 100ms LCP regression on the product page can reduce conversion by 1-2%.

useCases.title: Splunk RUM JavaScript Error Rate by Page
useCases.value: Frontend JavaScript errors — unhandled exceptions, failed API calls, resource loading failures — directly degrade user experience but are invisible to backend monitoring. RUM captures these errors with full stack traces, page URL, browser, and user session context. Tracking JS error rate by page detects regressions after deployments, identifies browser-specific bugs, and quantifies the user impact of frontend failures that backend health checks miss entirely.

useCases.title: Splunk Synthetic Monitoring Multi-Step Transaction SLA
useCases.value: Beyond simple pass/fail synthetic checks (UC-13.3.10), multi-step browser transactions test complete user workflows — login, search, add-to-cart, checkout. Step-level timing trends reveal which step is degrading: if the login step takes 500ms longer in one geography, that points to a regional identity provider issue. Transaction SLA tracking quantifies end-user experience commitments and provides evidence for SLA breach discussions with internal service owners or external vendors.

useCases.title: Splunk Observability Cloud Detector Health
useCases.value: Observability Cloud detectors (alerts) degrade silently: a detector may be permanently muted, have no recent data feeding its signal, fire so frequently it's ignored (alert fatigue), or have a condition that can never trigger due to metric name changes. Monitoring detector health ensures the alerting layer that protects production services is itself healthy — preventing the dangerous situation where teams believe they're covered by alerts that haven't actually fired or evaluated in months.

useCases.title: RED Metrics Dashboard Template (Rate, Errors, Duration)
useCases.value: The RED method (Rate, Errors, Duration) is the standard SRE pattern for monitoring request-driven services. This template UC provides a reusable SPL pattern applicable to any HTTP/gRPC service instrumented with OTel — producing the three essential metrics that answer "is this service healthy right now?" Having a standardized RED pattern ensures every team monitors their services consistently, enabling fleet-wide comparison and prioritization.

app: Splunk Distribution of OpenTelemetry Collector (hostmetrics receiver)
useCases.title: USE Method for Infrastructure (Utilization, Saturation, Errors)
useCases.value: The USE method (Utilization, Saturation, Errors) is the standard SRE pattern for monitoring resource-driven systems (CPU, memory, disk, network). While individual infrastructure UCs exist across cat-01 and cat-05, this template consolidates all three signals per resource into a unified view that answers "is this resource the bottleneck?" Having the USE framework as a structured pattern ensures systematic coverage — teams often monitor utilization but miss saturation (the queue) and errors (the failures).

useCases.title: Golden Signals Composite Health per Service
useCases.value: Google SRE's four Golden Signals — Latency, Traffic, Errors, Saturation — provide a complete view of service health when combined into a composite score. Individual signal monitoring exists across various UCs, but a composite score enables service-level comparison and prioritization: when 20 services degrade simultaneously during an incident, the composite score instantly ranks which services are worst-affected. This is particularly valuable for non-ITSI deployments that lack ITSI's built-in service health scoring.

useCases.title: SLO Definition and Multi-Window Burn Rate Alerting
useCases.value: Simple error rate thresholds create two failure modes: too sensitive (alert on every transient error) or too lenient (miss sustained degradation). Google SRE's multi-window burn rate alerting solves this by measuring how fast you're consuming your error budget across multiple time windows. A fast burn (5min/1hr window) catches severe outages immediately; a slow burn (30min/6hr window) catches gradual degradation that compounds. This structured approach replaces ad-hoc threshold alerting with mathematically rigorous SLO-based alerting.

useCases.title: Error Budget Policy Enforcement
useCases.value: An SLO without enforcement is just a dashboard. Error budget policies define what happens when a service exhausts its error budget: feature freeze, mandatory reliability work, postmortem requirement, or escalation to engineering leadership. Tracking error budget consumption per service per period and automatically flagging services that have exhausted their budget creates accountability — transforming SLOs from aspirational targets into governance mechanisms that balance feature velocity with reliability investment.

useCases.title: Observability Data Volume and Cost Attribution
useCases.value: Observability platforms charge by data volume (metrics data points, trace spans, log GB). Without attribution, a single team's misconfigured debug logging or high-cardinality metrics can spike the monthly bill by 40% while no one knows who caused it. Attributing observability data volume to services, teams, and environments enables FinOps governance — teams that generate the most telemetry bear the cost, creating incentive to instrument efficiently rather than indiscriminately.

useCases.title: Observability Cardinality Explosion Detection
useCases.value: Metric cardinality — the number of unique time series — is the hidden cost driver of observability platforms. Adding a high-cardinality label like `user_id` or `request_id` to a metric can create millions of unique time series, overwhelming TSDB backends and causing query timeouts, memory exhaustion, and unexpected cost spikes. Detecting cardinality explosions before they impact platform stability prevents outages in the observability infrastructure itself.

useCases.title: Instrumentation Coverage Audit
useCases.value: You can't debug what you can't see. Services without OTel instrumentation are "dark" — when they fail, you diagnose from the outside using downstream error messages and infrastructure metrics, adding 30-60 minutes to MTTR. Measuring instrumentation coverage per team (what percentage of their services emit traces, metrics, and logs with trace context) drives observability maturity programs with data rather than mandates. A coverage target of 90% for critical services creates measurable accountability.

useCases.title: Telemetry Signal Freshness and Staleness
useCases.value: A service that stops emitting metrics or traces could mean two very different things: the service is down (infrastructure problem requiring immediate response) or the instrumentation broke (observability gap requiring engineering fix). Monitoring signal freshness — how recently each service last emitted each signal type — distinguishes these cases. If infrastructure monitoring shows the service is running but traces stopped, the instrumentation broke. If both stop, the service is likely down. Without freshness monitoring, instrumentation failures go unnoticed until the next incident when debugging tools fail.

useCases.title: HVAC Performance Monitoring
useCases.value: HVAC issues in data centers risk equipment damage; in buildings they affect occupant comfort and energy costs.

useCases.title: Elevator/Equipment Health
useCases.value: Equipment fault codes enable predictive maintenance, reducing downtime and extending equipment life.

useCases.title: Environmental Compliance
useCases.value: Temperature/humidity exceedances in data centers risk equipment damage; in labs they invalidate experiments. Compliance monitoring is mandatory.

useCases.title: LoRaWAN Gateway Health
useCases.value: Gateway uplink/downlink success rate and RSSI trending indicate network coverage and reliability. Degraded gateways cause packet loss and affect IoT application availability.

useCases.title: Modbus Device Communication Failure Rate
useCases.value: Poll timeout tracking across Modbus TCP/RTU slaves identifies communication failures before they impact process control. High failure rates indicate network issues, slave overload, or misconfiguration.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Server Session Count and Subscription Health
useCases.value: Session limits and subscription keep-alive failures indicate OPC-UA server capacity and client connectivity. Exceeding session limits or subscription failures cause data gaps and break real-time monitoring.

useCases.title: SNMP Trap Storm Detection
useCases.value: Trap floods overwhelm collectors and obscure real faults; rapid detection enables rate limiting and upstream device triage.

useCases.title: Device MIB Polling Failures
useCases.value: Failed GET/GETNEXT/WALK cycles mean stale metrics and blind spots in capacity management.

useCases.title: Firmware Version Compliance Across Fleet
useCases.value: Known-bad IOS/NX-OS/IOS-XE builds expose the network to CVEs; compliance reporting supports change windows.

useCases.title: Environmental Sensor Threshold Alerts
useCases.value: Rack intake temperature and humidity from SNMP sensors protect IT and edge equipment from thermal damage.

useCases.title: SNMPv3 Authentication Failures
useCases.value: Auth failures indicate credential rotation gaps, brute force, or misconfigured collectors.

useCases.title: Temperature Sensor Threshold Alerts (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Alerts when environmental temperatures exceed safe thresholds to prevent equipment damage.

useCases.title: Humidity Monitoring and Dew Point Tracking (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Monitors humidity levels to ensure optimal conditions for equipment and prevent moisture damage.

useCases.title: Door Open/Close Event Detection and Alerts (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Tracks door access events for security and facility monitoring.

useCases.title: Water Leak Detection and Flood Alerts (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Immediately detects water leaks to prevent equipment damage and business interruption.

useCases.title: Power Monitoring and Electrical Load Analysis (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Tracks electrical power consumption and load to identify anomalies and plan upgrades.

useCases.title: Air Quality and CO2 Monitoring (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Monitors indoor air quality to ensure safe working conditions.

useCases.title: Ambient Noise Level Monitoring and Trend Analysis (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Tracks noise levels to ensure comfortable working environment and detect anomalies.

useCases.title: Indoor Climate Trending and HVAC Optimization (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Analyzes temperature and humidity trends to optimize HVAC system efficiency.

useCases.title: Environmental Sensor Battery Health and Replacement Alerts (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Tracks sensor battery levels to ensure sensors remain operational and schedule replacements.

useCases.title: Sensor Connectivity and Heartbeat Monitoring (Meraki MT)
useCases.value: Ensures all sensors maintain connectivity and operational status.

useCases.title: AHU Supply Air Temperature Deviation
useCases.value: Air Handling Unit supply air temperature drifting from setpoint indicates coil fouling, valve failures, or economizer faults — wasting energy and degrading occupant comfort. Catching deviations early prevents complaints and energy waste.

useCases.title: VAV Box Damper Position Stuck Detection
useCases.value: Approximately 30% of VAV boxes operate with faults in typical buildings. A stuck damper actuator causes a zone to receive constant airflow regardless of demand — wasting 15-25% of HVAC energy per affected zone and creating hot/cold complaints.

useCases.title: Chiller Plant COP Efficiency Trending
useCases.value: Chiller plants consume 30-50% of total building energy. Tracking Coefficient of Performance (COP) identifies degradation from condenser fouling, refrigerant loss, or suboptimal sequencing — enabling 15-30% cooling energy savings.

useCases.title: Cooling Tower Approach Temperature Trending
useCases.value: Approach temperature (difference between condenser water leaving the tower and outdoor wet bulb) reveals cooling tower effectiveness. Rising approach indicates fill media fouling, fan issues, or scale buildup — directly impacting chiller efficiency.

useCases.title: HVAC Setpoint Override Frequency and Duration
useCases.value: Frequent manual setpoint overrides by occupants or operators indicate either comfort issues or poor control tuning. Tracking override patterns helps identify problem zones and quantifies energy waste from overrides that persist beyond work hours.

useCases.title: Economizer Free Cooling Hours Tracking
useCases.value: Economizer mode uses outside air for free cooling when conditions permit, saving significant compressor energy. Tracking actual free cooling hours vs available hours reveals malfunctioning dampers, faulty enthalpy sensors, or misconfigured switchover points.

useCases.title: Building Energy Consumption Intensity (kWh/m²)
useCases.value: Energy Use Intensity (EUI) in kWh per square meter is the standard benchmark for building energy performance. Tracking EUI trending and comparing across buildings reveals efficiency opportunities and supports ENERGY STAR, LEED, and ESG reporting.

useCases.title: Sub-Meter Energy Distribution by System
useCases.value: Sub-metering breaks total energy into HVAC, lighting, plug loads, and other systems. Knowing which system consumes the most energy directs efficiency investments where they'll have the biggest impact — typically HVAC at 40-60%.

useCases.title: After-Hours Energy Waste Detection
useCases.value: Buildings typically waste 20-30% of energy outside occupied hours from HVAC systems running on override, lights left on, or equipment not in unoccupied mode. Detecting after-hours energy above baseline enables quick wins with minimal investment.

useCases.title: Peak Demand Shaving Effectiveness
useCases.value: Utility demand charges based on peak 15-minute kW draw can represent 30-50% of a commercial building's electric bill. Monitoring peak demand and evaluating load-shedding effectiveness helps control costs and supports demand response programs.

useCases.title: Lighting Schedule Compliance and Override Tracking
useCases.value: Lighting left on outside scheduled hours wastes 10-20% of lighting energy. Tracking schedule compliance and manual override patterns identifies zones where schedules need adjustment or occupancy sensors should be added.

useCases.title: Elevator Trip Count and Usage Trending
useCases.value: Elevator trip counts, floor-by-floor usage patterns, and duty cycles drive maintenance scheduling and modernization planning. High-traffic elevators need more frequent service. Usage data also informs tenant space planning and lobby redesign.

useCases.title: Elevator Door Fault Frequency and Prediction
useCases.value: Door faults are the most common elevator malfunction and the leading cause of entrapments. Monitoring door close force, cycle time, and motor amperage detects deteriorating door systems 2-6 weeks before failure — preventing passenger entrapments and service calls.

useCases.title: Elevator Wait Time and Service Quality
useCases.value: Average wait time is the primary measure of elevator service quality visible to occupants. Industry target is under 30 seconds for office buildings. Excessive wait times indicate traffic imbalance, out-of-service cars, or poor dispatching algorithms.

useCases.title: Water Consumption Trending and Anomaly Detection
useCases.value: Undetected water leaks can waste thousands of liters daily and cause structural damage. Continuous flow monitoring detects leaks, running toilets, and irrigation faults within hours rather than the weeks it takes for a utility bill to reveal problems.

useCases.title: Domestic Hot Water Temperature Compliance (Legionella Prevention)
useCases.value: Legionella bacteria thrive in water between 20-45°C. Building codes require domestic hot water storage above 60°C and distribution above 50°C. Temperature drops below these thresholds create serious health risks and regulatory violations.

useCases.title: Cooling Tower Water Chemistry Monitoring
useCases.value: Cooling tower water chemistry (conductivity, pH, biocide levels) directly impacts heat transfer efficiency and equipment life. Scale buildup from poor chemistry increases chiller energy by 2-5% per mm of scale and accelerates corrosion.

useCases.title: Fire Alarm Panel Zone Health and Event Monitoring
useCases.value: Fire alarm panel trouble conditions (ground faults, open circuits, dirty detectors) must be resolved promptly to maintain life safety protection. Centralizing fire panel events enables multi-building oversight and faster trouble resolution.

app: Fire alarm panel integration (valve tamper switches connected to panel)
useCases.title: Sprinkler System Valve Tamper and Supervisory Monitoring
useCases.value: Closed or partially closed sprinkler valves are the number one reason sprinkler systems fail to operate during a fire. Valve tamper switches provide immediate notification when a valve position changes — NFPA 25 requires monitoring.

app: Fire pump controller (via syslog or serial gateway)
useCases.title: Fire Pump Controller Status and Run Monitoring
useCases.value: Fire pumps must be ready to operate instantly during a fire. Controller monitoring tracks pump starts, run duration, phase voltage, and jockey pump cycling. Excessive jockey pump cycling often indicates system leaks that degrade firefighting readiness.

useCases.title: BACnet Controller Communication Health
useCases.value: BACnet controllers are the brains of building automation — each manages a zone, floor, or system. Communication loss means affected areas run in fallback mode with no remote visibility or control. Monitoring network health catches issues before occupants notice.

useCases.title: BMS Alarm Flood Detection and Suppression
useCases.value: A single equipment failure (e.g., chiller trip) can generate hundreds of cascading BMS alarms across downstream systems — overwhelming operators and burying the root cause. Detecting alarm floods and identifying the source event reduces mean time to resolve.

useCases.title: Parking Occupancy Trending and Capacity Planning
useCases.value: Real-time parking occupancy data optimizes space utilization, reduces circling time, and informs expansion or reduction decisions. Trending occupancy by day-of-week and time helps set pricing tiers and plan EV charging capacity.

useCases.title: EV Charging Station Availability and Utilization
useCases.value: EV charging infrastructure is rapidly growing in commercial buildings. Monitoring station availability, session duration, and energy delivery helps right-size charging capacity, identify broken stations, and plan electrical load management.

useCases.title: Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) Index Monitoring
useCases.value: Post-pandemic, indoor air quality is a top tenant concern. CO2 concentration is a direct proxy for ventilation effectiveness and occupant density. PM2.5, VOCs, and CO2 together create a composite IAQ index that supports WELL Building and RESET Air certification.

useCases.title: Carbon Emissions Tracking from Building Operations (Scope 1+2)
useCases.value: ESG reporting increasingly requires Scope 1 (on-site combustion) and Scope 2 (purchased electricity) carbon emissions tracking. Automating carbon calculations from utility meter data provides real-time emissions dashboards and supports Science Based Targets.

useCases.title: PLC/RTU Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Controller failures halt industrial processes. Monitoring CPU, memory, and communication status prevents unplanned downtime.

useCases.title: Process Variable Anomalies
useCases.value: Process variables (pressure, flow, temperature) outside normal ranges indicate equipment failure or process upset. Early detection prevents safety incidents.

useCases.title: Safety System Activation
useCases.value: Safety system activations (ESD, interlocks) indicate dangerous conditions. Each activation requires investigation and documentation.

useCases.title: Network Segmentation Monitoring
useCases.value: IT/OT network boundary violations create cybersecurity risk to critical infrastructure. Continuous monitoring validates segmentation.

useCases.title: Firmware Version Tracking
useCases.value: OT devices with outdated firmware are vulnerable to exploitation. Inventory tracking supports patching during maintenance windows.

useCases.title: Unauthorized Access Detection
useCases.value: Unauthorized access to ICS systems could lead to physical damage or safety incidents. Detection is critical for industrial cybersecurity.

useCases.title: Modbus TCP Anomaly Detection
useCases.value: Unusual read/write rates or register ranges can indicate process upset or malicious manipulation.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Session Abuse
useCases.value: Excessive sessions or anonymous binds from new clients can indicate scanning or unauthorized access.

useCases.title: PLC Firmware Change Detection
useCases.value: Unexpected firmware changes on PLCs can be maintenance errors or malicious reprogramming.

useCases.title: ICS Protocol Violation Alerts
useCases.value: Malformed DNP3/Modbus/Profinet frames or wrong L4 ports indicate misconfiguration or attacks.

useCases.title: NERC CIP Compliance Checks
useCases.value: Evidence of electronic access controls, logging, and change management for bulk electric systems.

useCases.title: Historian Data Integrity
useCases.value: Gaps or duplicated timestamps in historian feeds break batch quality and regulatory reporting.

useCases.title: Safety Instrumented System Monitoring
useCases.value: SIS trips, bypasses, and diagnostics demand immediate visibility and audit trails.

useCases.title: HMI Unauthorized Access
useCases.value: HMIs should only be reachable from jump hosts; direct access from corporate networks is a red flag.

useCases.title: Control Loop Deviation
useCases.value: PV diverging from SP with saturated output indicates tuning issues or actuator faults.

useCases.title: Process Variable Trending
useCases.value: Slow drift before alarm limits supports predictive maintenance and energy optimization.

useCases.title: ICS Network Segmentation Violations
useCases.value: Hosts in wrong VLANs or east-west traffic across zones violates Purdue model and IEC 62443.

useCases.title: Engineering Workstation Anomaly
useCases.value: USB inserts, new binaries, or remote sessions on EWS workstations are high-risk in OT.

useCases.title: OT Asset External Communication Detection
useCases.value: PLCs, HMIs, or sensors initiating outbound sessions to the internet or untrusted zones indicate misconfiguration, malware, or pivot from IT — a top IEC 62443 / NERC CIP concern.

useCases.title: OT Protocol Port Monitoring
useCases.value: Unexpected Modbus, DNP3, or EtherNet/IP ports on non-asset IPs reveal rogue devices or scanning.

useCases.title: Removable Media in OT Detection
useCases.value: USB events on HMIs or engineering stations violate many site policies and are common malware vectors.

useCases.value: Baselines permitted jump-server, patch, and historian replication across the Purdue boundary; flags new apps or volume spikes.

useCases.title: ICS Change Management Compliance
useCases.value: Logic downloads, firmware pushes, or HMI project changes without a linked work order break IEC 62443 SR-7 / internal change policy.

useCases.title: Production Line Downtime Tracking

useCases.title: EDI Acknowledgement Monitoring

useCases.title: Supplier Delivery Performance
useCases.value: On-time delivery % and lead-time variance from ASN/OTIF feeds support supplier scorecards and production planning.

useCases.title: Vibration & Motion Monitoring

useCases.value: Audits all HMI operator actions (setpoint changes, equipment starts/stops) for compliance and root cause analysis.

useCases.title: Cellular Connectivity Quality & Signal Strength Monitoring
useCases.value: Tracks LTE/4G signal strength and network latency to predict connectivity issues and plan network upgrades.

useCases.title: Edge Hub Resource Capacity Planning & CPU/Memory Utilization
useCases.value: Prevents Edge Hub performance degradation and data loss by tracking resource utilization and planning for container resource allocation.

useCases.title: Configuration Drift Detection Across Fleet
useCases.value: Ensures all Edge Hubs in a fleet maintain consistent configuration (MQTT topics, OPC-UA endpoints, polling intervals) to prevent data inconsistencies.

useCases.title: Local Backlog Monitoring & Data Loss Prevention
useCases.value: Prevents silent data loss by monitoring local SQLite backlog capacity and alerting before data is discarded.

useCases.value: Detects when sensors exceed acceptable calibration drift to trigger preventive recalibration and ensure measurement accuracy.

useCases.title: Light Sensor Ambient Light Level Anomaly Detection

useCases.value: Ensures MQTT message delivery reliability by tracking topic latency and detecting lost or delayed messages.

useCases.title: Temperature Sensor Response Time Validation & Lag Detection
useCases.value: Validates temperature sensor response time to ensure rapid detection of thermal events (e.g., fire detection latency < 30 seconds).

useCases.title: Smart Sensor Fleet Health

useCases.title: Environmental Monitoring

useCases.title: Asset Tracking
useCases.value: Real-time asset location reduces search time, prevents loss, and enables utilization optimization.

useCases.title: Home Automation Monitoring
useCases.value: Smart home monitoring provides energy usage insights, security awareness, and automation troubleshooting.

useCases.value: IoT devices are frequently targeted for botnets. Outdated firmware creates network security risks.

useCases.title: IoT Device Connectivity and Last-Seen Monitoring
useCases.value: Devices that stop reporting indicate failure, network issues, or tampering. Last-seen monitoring ensures fleet visibility and rapid response to outages.

useCases.title: OT Protocol Anomaly and Unauthorized Command Detection
useCases.value: Unusual Modbus/OPC-UA/DNP3 commands or write operations can indicate attack or misconfiguration. Detection supports OT security and safety.

useCases.title: Sensor Calibration and Drift Detection
useCases.value: Sensor drift causes incorrect control and compliance issues. Detecting drift against reference or peer sensors supports maintenance and data quality.

useCases.title: Gateway and Edge Node Resource Utilization
useCases.value: Overloaded gateways drop telemetry or delay processing. Monitoring CPU, memory, and queue depth ensures edge reliability and capacity planning.

useCases.title: IoT Data Pipeline Throughput and Latency
