useCases.value: Mesh coordinators and gateways aggregate low-power sensors; their health affects entire buildings.

useCases.title: MQTT Topic Message Rate and Subscription Health
useCases.value: Per-topic message rate and subscriber count indicate whether sensors and downstream consumers are healthy. Sudden drops mean a publisher or subscription failed; spikes can indicate a runaway device or replay.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Server Connection and Session Count
useCases.value: OPC-UA session count and connection state indicate whether Edge Hub or gateways are successfully bound to PLCs/servers. Lost sessions create data gaps and break real-time monitoring.

useCases.title: Edge Hub MQTT Broker Client Disconnections
useCases.value: Frequent client disconnections or reconnect storms indicate network issues, broker overload, or misconfigured keep-alive. Monitoring supports stability and capacity planning.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Node Value Change Rate and Anomaly
useCases.value: PLC tag value change rate and distribution indicate normal process behavior. Sudden change in rate or value distribution can signal sensor fault, process upset, or cyber event.

useCases.title: Edge Hub to Cloud HEC Forwarding Backlog
useCases.value: When Edge Hub loses connectivity to Splunk, data backs up locally (e.g. 3M sensor points in SQLite). Backlog growth and drain rate indicate risk of data loss and recovery time.

useCases.title: MQTT Retain and Last Will Message Audit
useCases.value: Retained messages and Last Will payloads can contain sensitive state. Auditing who published retain/LWT and when supports change control and security review.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Alarms and Events Queue Depth
useCases.value: OPC-UA alarm/event queues that grow indicate slow consumption or overflow risk. Overflow can drop critical alarms; depth trending supports connector and gateway sizing.

useCases.title: MQTT QoS 0/1/2 Delivery and Drops
useCases.value: QoS 0 messages can be dropped under load; QoS 1/2 add overhead. Tracking delivery by QoS and drop rate supports SLA and broker tuning.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Certificate Expiration and Trust
useCases.value: Expired or untrusted OPC-UA certificates break secure connections and prevent data collection. Proactive monitoring avoids blind spots after certificate rollover failures.

useCases.title: Edge Hub Local Storage and SQLite Backlog
useCases.value: Edge Hub stores backlog in SQLite when disconnected. Disk usage and backlog size must stay within limits (e.g. 3M sensor points) to avoid data loss and device lockup.

useCases.title: MQTT Authentication Failure and ACL Denials
useCases.value: Failed MQTT logins and publish/subscribe denials indicate credential abuse, misconfiguration, or attack. Monitoring supports access control and incident response.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Subscription Latency and Sampling Overrun
useCases.value: High subscription latency or sampling overrun (server missing sample interval) degrades real-time visibility. Tracking supports connector and server tuning.

useCases.title: Edge Hub Container Health (MQTT/OPC-UA Modules)
useCases.value: Edge Hub runs MQTT broker and OPC-UA connector as modules. Container restarts or OOM kills cause data gaps and require investigation.

useCases.title: MQTT TLS Handshake and Cipher Compliance
useCases.value: TLS handshake failures or weak ciphers indicate misconfiguration or downgrade attacks. Monitoring ensures encrypted MQTT and policy compliance.

useCases.title: OPC-UA Write and Permission Denials
useCases.value: Unauthorized write attempts or permission denials can indicate misconfiguration, abuse, or attack. Auditing supports least-privilege and security review.

useCases.title: HiveMQ Cluster Node Health and Split-Brain Detection
useCases.value: MQTT broker cluster faults and split-brain conditions fragment subscriptions and retained state; early detection avoids cross-site messaging black holes.

useCases.title: MQTT Shared Subscription Load Distribution
useCases.value: Shared subscriptions should balance load across consumers; skew indicates stuck consumers or broker-side dispatch issues that inflate latency.

useCases.title: HiveMQ Retained Message Store Growth
useCases.value: Retained messages accumulate with misconfigured publishers; growth risks disk exhaustion and slower broker startup, especially at OT edge with constrained storage.

useCases.title: MQTT Client Disconnect Reason Analysis
useCases.value: Categorized disconnect reasons separate clean shutdowns from timeouts, kicks, and protocol errors — shortening MTTR for unstable OT clients.

useCases.title: HiveMQ Extension Execution Errors
useCases.value: HiveMQ extensions (enterprise integrations, custom interceptors) can fail independently; tracking exceptions prevents silent drops in policy enforcement and data enrichment.

useCases.title: MQTT Topic Tree Depth and Fan-Out Analysis
useCases.value: Deep topic hierarchies and high fan-out increase broker memory and ACL evaluation costs; trending complexity helps right-size clusters and topic design reviews.

useCases.title: HiveMQ License Utilization Trending
useCases.value: Connection growth toward license limits causes hard rejections during peaks; trending utilization supports procurement decisions before production brownouts.

useCases.title: S7comm PLC Read/Write Operation Monitoring
useCases.value: Unexpected write-heavy traffic to Siemens PLCs can indicate tampering or mis-engineered automation; tracking read versus write ratios supports least-privilege engineering and early detection of process-impacting changes.

useCases.title: S7comm Program Upload/Download Detection
useCases.value: PLC program upload/download changes process logic and safety envelopes; correlating these events with change tickets prevents unauthorized logic swaps that could disrupt operations or bypass interlocks.

useCases.title: S7comm CPU State Change Detection
useCases.value: CPU stop/start or mode transitions can halt a line or leave a PLC in an unsafe state; detecting them from the wire supports both troubleshooting and detection of malicious or accidental operational disruption.

useCases.title: S7comm Unauthorized Function Block Access
useCases.value: Access attempts to protected OB/FB/FC blocks may indicate credential abuse or ladder tampering; monitoring errors and targeted function names supports defense-in-depth around safety-related code.

useCases.title: Modbus Function Code Distribution Audit
useCases.value: Diagnostics and coil forcing are high-impact Modbus operations; a sudden shift in function-code mix can signal scanning, misuse, or a compromised HMI.

useCases.title: Modbus Register Value Change Tracking
useCases.value: Covert changes to holding registers can alter setpoints or interlocks; comparing matched request/response values highlights tampering distinct from normal operator writes.

useCases.title: Modbus Device Identification Enumeration (FC 43 / 0x2B)
useCases.value: Read Device Identification (FC 0x2B) is a common reconnaissance step; bursts from non-inventory hosts often precede targeted attacks or rogue integration attempts.

useCases.title: DNP3 Unsolicited Response Monitoring
useCases.value: Unsolicited responses carry event-driven telemetry; abnormal volume or timing can indicate flooding, misconfiguration, or spoofed outstations affecting SCADA visibility.

useCases.title: DNP3 Control Relay Output Block (CROB) Tracking
useCases.value: CROB select/operate sequences directly actuate breakers and outputs; a full audit trail is required for NERC CIP-style reviews and post-incident forensics.

useCases.title: DNP3 Cold/Warm Restart Detection
useCases.value: Restart commands to outstations reset application context and can interrupt protection; unexpected restarts may follow malware or operator error.

useCases.title: EtherNet/IP CIP Service Request Audit
useCases.value: Unusual CIP services (e.g., configuration writes) against controllers can precede firmware or logic manipulation; service baselines highlight drift from normal automation behavior.

useCases.title: EtherNet/IP Unregistered Session Detection
useCases.value: EtherNet/IP sessions are normally established with explicit registration; traffic that skips expected session setup may indicate tooling errors, bypass attempts, or non-compliant devices on the plant floor.

useCases.title: EtherNet/IP I/O Implicit Messaging Anomaly
useCases.value: Implicit I/O carries real-time control data; sudden changes in payload size or timing can signal cable issues, configuration drift, or injection attempts affecting deterministic control.

useCases.title: IEC 104 Interrogation Command Monitoring
useCases.value: General interrogation and clock synchronization (types 100 and 103) can be abused for reconnaissance or time skew; auditing masters against expected scan behavior supports grid and plant operational integrity.

useCases.title: IEC 104 Spontaneous Value Change Tracking
useCases.value: Monitoring spontaneous updates helps distinguish normal process swings from stale data or spoofed telemetry that could mask a physical fault.

useCases.title: IEC 104 Clock Synchronization Deviation
useCases.value: Time drift between master and outstation complicates event ordering and SOE correlation; detecting skew supports NERC-style evidence of synchronized operations.

useCases.title: BACnet Object Access Audit
useCases.value: Writes to analog outputs, schedules, or life-safety objects can change building or process environmental limits; auditing ReadProperty/WriteProperty supports both cyber and operational accountability.

useCases.title: BACnet Who-Is Broadcast Storm Detection
useCases.value: Excessive Who-Is/I-Am discovery floods MS/TP-to-IP bridges and can indicate misconfigured devices, loops, or active scanning that degrades BMS responsiveness.

useCases.title: HART-IP Command 48 Additional Status Monitoring
useCases.value: HART command 48 returns extended device status; tracking additional status fields helps catch sensor faults or configuration issues before they affect closed-loop control.

useCases.title: Unknown Protocol on OT VLAN Detection
useCases.value: Non-whitelisted protocols on ICS segments often indicate shadow IT, dual-homed misconfigurations, or tunneling that bypasses zone policies—each can bridge IT threats into OT.

useCases.title: Litmus Edge Gateway Connectivity Health
useCases.value: Gateway offline events stop OT data from reaching Splunk; early detection reduces blind spots in plant visibility.

useCases.title: PLC Tag Data Ingestion Validation
useCases.value: Missing or silent tag streams break dashboards, historians, and ML models; validating expected tags catches connector or network regressions before production impact.

useCases.title: Edge-to-Splunk Data Pipeline Latency
useCases.value: End-to-end latency distinguishes edge capture delays from Splunk indexing backlog; spikes indicate broker saturation, HEC backpressure, or clock skew.

useCases.title: Production Sensor Data Completeness Audit
useCases.value: Stale or missing sensor readings invalidate safety and quality analytics; completeness audits align telemetry coverage with regulatory expectations for critical measurements.

useCases.title: Litmus Edge Device Inventory Drift
useCases.value: Unexpected devices or disappearing assets indicate misconfiguration or unauthorized connectivity; drift detection supports CMDB accuracy and OT security reviews.

useCases.title: Edge Data Transformation Error Rate
useCases.value: Transformation and normalization failures silently drop or corrupt OT fields; tracking error rates ties engineering changes to ingestion health.

useCases.title: Multi-Site Litmus Edge Fleet Health
useCases.value: Aggregating gateway health by site highlights WAN issues, deployment drift, and capacity hotspots across plants without per-host manual checks.

useCases.title: Litmus Edge Connector Authentication Monitoring
useCases.value: HEC token leakage, rotation mistakes, or clock skew cause auth failures that stop ingestion; monitoring auth errors accelerates rotation and prevents silent data gaps.

useCases.title: Centralized Model Retraining for Industrial Sensor ML (DSDL)
useCases.value: Edge-deployed ML models (autoencoder anomaly detection, XGBoost predictive maintenance, CNN visual inspection) degrade over time as equipment ages, processes change, and seasonal conditions shift. Centralized retraining in Splunk aggregates sensor data from all edge gateways, trains updated models via DSDL containers, and tracks model drift — ensuring edge predictions stay accurate without requiring data science expertise at each plant site.

app: optional Splunk OTel for OT gateways
useCases.title: Device Fleet Online Rate Trending
useCases.value: The share of devices reporting on schedule is a leading indicator of network, power, or gateway issues before production KPIs degrade; trending over 30 days shows whether fixes stick across sites.

useCases.title: Sensor Data Quality Trending
useCases.value: Missing or stale readings break historians, dashboards, and ML features; daily trending exposes ingestion gaps early so teams can fix collectors, radios, or brokers before safety or quality thresholds are blind.

useCases.title: OEE Trending
useCases.value: Overall Equipment Effectiveness summarizes availability, performance, and quality; weekly or monthly trends show whether maintenance programs and changeovers are improving plant output without waiting for quarterly business reviews.

useCases.title: Predictive Maintenance Alert Volume Trending
useCases.value: ML-driven anomaly counts should rise when equipment drifts but should fall after maintenance; tracking weekly volume validates model calibration and catches alert fatigue or broken scoring pipelines.

useCases.title: OT Asset Discovery and Inventory Tracking
useCases.value: You cannot secure what you do not know exists. OT network security platforms (Cisco Cyber Vision, Nozomi Guardian) passively discover every device on your OT network via deep packet inspection of industrial protocols — PLCs, HMIs, drives, field devices — and builds an always-current inventory with vendor, model, firmware, serial number, and rack slot. This eliminates manual spreadsheets and provides the foundation for all other OT security use cases.

useCases.title: New OT Device Detection Alert
useCases.value: Any new device appearing on a baselined OT network is a potential threat — rogue devices, unauthorized laptops, or attacker implants. OT security platforms detect new components automatically and generate alerts. Immediate alerting enables rapid investigation before a threat can spread.

useCases.title: OT Asset Vulnerability Detection and CVE Tracking
useCases.value: OT security platforms automatically match discovered OT assets against known CVEs, generating vulnerability alerts with CVE ID, CVSS score, and affected component. This eliminates manual vulnerability scanning in sensitive OT environments where active scanners can disrupt processes.

useCases.title: OT Asset Risk Score Monitoring
useCases.value: OT security platforms calculate composite risk scores per device considering vulnerabilities, communication patterns, and security posture. Monitoring risk score changes over time shows whether your OT security posture is improving or degrading, and highlights which assets need immediate attention.

useCases.title: Baseline Deviation Detection
useCases.value: OT security platforms baseline normal network behavior — which devices talk to which, over what protocols, at what frequency. Deviations from baseline trigger alerts, detecting unauthorized communication changes, new data flows, or behavioral shifts that could indicate compromise or misconfiguration.

useCases.title: Snort IDS Threat Detection on OT Networks
useCases.value: OT security platforms include built-in IDS engines with threat intelligence updates to detect known threats — malware, C2 traffic, exploit attempts — crossing into OT networks. This provides signature-based threat detection without deploying separate IDS appliances in sensitive OT environments.

useCases.title: PLC Program Download/Upload Detection
useCases.value: Unauthorized PLC program changes can alter physical processes with safety implications. OT security platforms detect program download and upload events across industrial protocols (EtherNet/IP, S7, Modbus, Profinet) and generate Critical-severity alerts. Every program change must be verified against authorized change windows.

useCases.title: Controller Firmware Activation Monitoring
useCases.value: Firmware activation on a controller changes the software running the physical process. Unauthorized firmware changes are a key indicator of advanced OT attacks (e.g., Stuxnet-style). OT security platforms detect firmware activation events across supported industrial protocols and generate Critical-severity alerts.

useCases.title: Forced Variable Detection in OT Processes
useCases.value: Forcing a variable in a PLC overrides the normal program logic — the variable holds a fixed value regardless of what the control program calculates. While sometimes used legitimately during maintenance, forced variables left active in production can mask sensor readings and bypass safety logic. OT security platforms detect forced variable events with variable name and value.

useCases.title: Control Action Monitoring on Industrial Assets
useCases.value: OT security platforms track control action events when a control system modifies process variables — setpoint changes, valve commands, motor start/stop. Monitoring these actions detects unauthorized process manipulation and provides an audit trail for root cause analysis of production incidents.

useCases.title: Controller Mode Change Detection
useCases.value: OT security platforms detect when controllers are placed into online, offline, force, or run/stop modes — each a Critical-severity event. A controller taken offline stops controlling its physical process. An unauthorized mode change could halt production, disable safety systems, or prepare for a more destructive attack.

useCases.title: New Communication Flow Detection
useCases.value: In a stable OT environment, the set of communication flows between devices should be predictable. OT security platforms generate alerts when a previously unseen protocol flow appears between two components. New FTP, HTTP, or SSH flows in the control network may indicate lateral movement, data exfiltration, or unauthorized remote access tools.

useCases.title: Protocol Exception Monitoring
useCases.value: Protocol exceptions (`illegal-function`, `invalid-data-address`, malformed packets) detected by OT DPI platforms indicate either misconfigured devices, faulty communication, or active exploitation attempts. An attacker probing Modbus function codes will trigger `illegal-function` exceptions. Repeated exceptions from a single source warrant investigation.

useCases.title: OT Device Authentication Failure Detection
useCases.value: OT security platforms detect login failure events including the number of failed authentication attempts and the protocol used. Brute-force login attempts against HMIs, engineering workstations, or web-enabled controllers indicate credential-based attacks that could lead to unauthorized process control.

useCases.title: Admin Connection Detection to ICS Assets
useCases.value: OT security platforms detect administrative connections to industrial components — engineering sessions to PLCs, configuration access to field devices. These events identify who is connecting to which controller, enabling detection of unauthorized engineering access that could modify process logic.

useCases.title: Port Scan Detection on OT Networks
useCases.value: Port scanning is a reconnaissance technique used by attackers to map OT network topology and identify exploitable services. OT security platforms detect port scan events with scanner and target component identification. Port scans in OT networks are almost never legitimate and warrant immediate investigation.

useCases.title: Weak Encryption Detection in OT Communications
useCases.value: Many OT protocols use weak or no encryption. OT security platforms identify flows using deprecated TLS versions, weak ciphers, or unencrypted protocols where encryption should be used. This supports IEC 62443 compliance and prioritizes protocol hardening efforts.

useCases.title: SMB Protocol Activity in OT Networks
useCases.value: SMB (Server Message Block) traffic in OT networks is frequently associated with ransomware propagation (WannaCry, NotPetya) and lateral movement. OT security platforms detect SMB protocol events. Any SMB activity in pure control network segments is suspicious and may indicate an active threat.

useCases.title: Network Redundancy and HA Failover Events
useCases.value: OT security platforms detect network redundancy failover events and router HA state changes across industrial protocols. Frequent failovers indicate network instability that could disrupt real-time control. Unexpected failovers may also indicate denial-of-service attacks or physical cable issues.

useCases.title: Cyber Vision Sensor Health and Resource Monitoring
useCases.value: OT security sensors and appliances need monitoring themselves — high CPU, memory, or disk usage events fire when resources exceed thresholds. Degraded sensors may miss traffic, creating blind spots in OT visibility.

useCases.title: Cyber Vision Administration Audit Trail
useCases.value: All administrative actions in OT security platforms — user logins, configuration changes, sensor management, database operations — are logged. Maintaining an audit trail of who did what and when supports regulatory compliance (IEC 62443, NERC CIP) and insider threat detection.

useCases.title: IEC 62443 Zone and Conduit Compliance Monitoring
useCases.value: IEC 62443 requires industrial networks to be segmented into security zones connected by controlled conduits. OT security platforms help control engineers define these zones and automatically detect cross-zone traffic that violates conduit policies. Monitoring zone compliance ensures segmentation remains effective over time.

useCases.title: OT Event Severity Distribution and Security Posture Dashboard
useCases.value: A high-level view of all OT security events by severity and category provides security posture at a glance. Trending event volumes over time shows whether security is improving (fewer Critical/High events) or degrading. Supports CISO reporting and board-level OT security metrics.

useCases.title: OT Protocol Usage Analysis and Inventory
useCases.value: OT security platforms identify all industrial protocols in use across the OT network — Modbus, EtherNet/IP, Profinet, S7, BACnet, DNP3, IEC 104, OPC-UA, and dozens more. Understanding protocol distribution helps prioritize security investments, plan protocol-specific IDS rules, and identify legacy protocols that need migration.

useCases.title: Decode Failure and Malformed Packet Detection
useCases.value: OT security platforms generate decode failure events when their DPI engine encounters packets it cannot properly parse — potentially indicating protocol fuzzing attacks, corrupted communications, or deliberately malformed exploit payloads targeting OT devices. Sustained decode failures from a single source may indicate active exploitation attempts.

useCases.title: UPS Battery Health
useCases.value: UPS battery degradation is the single largest cause of unprotected power events. Proactive replacement prevents data center outages.

useCases.title: PDU Power per Rack
useCases.value: Per-rack power monitoring prevents circuit overloads and enables efficient rack placement for new equipment.

useCases.title: Power Redundancy Status
useCases.value: Loss of A/B feed redundancy means a single power failure will cause an outage. Immediate awareness enables emergency response.

useCases.title: Generator Test Results
useCases.value: Generators are the last line of defense during extended outages. Failed tests mean they may not start when needed.

useCases.title: PUE Calculation
useCases.value: Power Usage Effectiveness is the primary data center efficiency metric. Trending drives energy optimization and sustainability goals.

useCases.title: Circuit Breaker Trips
useCases.value: Breaker trips cause immediate power loss to affected equipment. Detection enables rapid response and root cause investigation.

useCases.title: APC PDU Outlet-Level Power Monitoring
useCases.value: Per-outlet current draw and on/off state on APC rack PDUs enables granular power attribution, remote outlet control verification, and identification of high-draw devices within a rack.

useCases.title: Generator Runtime and Fuel Level
useCases.value: Diesel generator monitoring for extended outages; fuel level and run hours ensure generators can sustain operations during prolonged utility failures.

useCases.title: Rack Power Density Trending
useCases.value: Watts per rack unit over time for capacity planning; identifies hot spots and supports safe equipment placement decisions.

useCases.title: UPS Battery Runtime Remaining
useCases.value: Minutes of runtime remaining under present load is the actionable metric for graceful shutdown sequencing during outages.

useCases.title: PDU Outlet-Level Power Draw
useCases.value: Per-outlet amps identify rogue devices and balance load across strips before branch trips.

useCases.title: Generator Fuel Level Monitoring
useCases.value: Tank level and burn rate determine how long the site can run off-grid; critical for extended utility failures.

useCases.title: Transfer Switch Events
useCases.value: ATS transitions between utility and generator must be logged for root cause of brief outages and equipment stress.

useCases.title: Power Factor Monitoring
useCases.value: Low PF increases utility demand charges and heats conductors; correction banks need verification.

useCases.title: PUE Efficiency Tracking vs Target
useCases.value: Comparing live PUE to annual design target drives mechanical optimization and executive reporting.

useCases.title: Breaker Panel Load Balancing
useCases.value: Uneven loading across panel phases causes neutral current and premature breaker wear.

useCases.title: UPS Self-Test Failure
useCases.value: Failed self-tests indicate battery or inverter faults before a real outage.

useCases.title: Generator Start Failure
useCases.value: Failed cranks or inability to reach rated speed leave the site on battery-only until resolved.

useCases.title: Power Redundancy Compliance (N+1)
useCases.value: Proves both A/B feeds and redundant UPS paths are energized and within load limits for loss-of-one scenarios.

useCases.title: PDU Branch Circuit Alerts
useCases.value: Branch breakers trip before mains; per-branch monitoring catches overload before rack outage.

useCases.title: Electrical Panel Phase Balancing
useCases.value: Panel-level phase balance differs from rack PDU balance; both matter for neutral harmonics and breaker life.

useCases.title: UPS Battery Monitoring
useCases.value: UPS battery failure during power loss causes complete outage. Proactive monitoring prevents unprotected power events.

useCases.title: Power Consumption Trending
useCases.value: Power consumption trending supports capacity planning, cost management, and sustainability reporting. Anomalies indicate equipment issues.

useCases.title: Rack PDU Load and Phase Balance
useCases.value: PDU overload or phase imbalance risks circuit trips and equipment failure. Monitoring supports capacity planning and safe load distribution.

useCases.title: Generator Run Hours and Maintenance Due
useCases.value: Generator maintenance based on run hours ensures reliability during outages. Tracking run hours and maintenance due dates avoids missed service.

useCases.title: Temperature Monitoring per Zone
useCases.value: Data center temperature exceedances risk equipment damage and unplanned shutdowns. Per-zone monitoring localizes issues.

useCases.title: Humidity Monitoring
useCases.value: Low humidity causes ESD risk; high humidity causes condensation. Maintaining 40-60% RH protects equipment.

useCases.title: CRAC/CRAH Unit Health
useCases.value: Cooling unit failures can cause rapid temperature rise. Monitoring operational status enables immediate response and failover.

useCases.title: Hot Aisle Temperature Trending
useCases.value: Hot aisle trends indicate cooling efficiency and capacity margin. Rising trends signal approaching cooling limits.

useCases.title: Water Leak Detection
useCases.value: Water in a data center causes immediate equipment damage and potential electrical hazards. Seconds matter in detection.

useCases.title: Cooling Capacity Planning
useCases.value: Trending cooling load vs capacity ensures adequate cooling for current and planned equipment deployments.

useCases.title: APC InRow / CRAC Unit Temperature Differential
useCases.value: Inlet/outlet delta-T indicating cooling effectiveness; low delta-T suggests bypass airflow or undersized cooling; high delta-T indicates effective heat removal.

useCases.title: CRAC Unit Failure and Alarm State
useCases.value: Explicit CRAC fault/alarm bits catch compressor and fan failures not visible in temperature alone.

useCases.title: Hot/Cold Aisle Temperature Delta
useCases.value: Low ΔT across containment indicates bypass airflow or insufficient airflow; high ΔT may signal restricted return.

useCases.title: Humidity Threshold Exceedance (ASHRAE)
useCases.value: Stricter alerting for short excursions supports tape media and corrosion-sensitive gear beyond static high/low limits.

useCases.title: Chiller Plant Efficiency (kW/ton)
useCases.value: Elevated kW/ton indicates fouling, low refrigerant, or poor tower performance.

useCases.title: Liquid Cooling Loop Pressure
useCases.value: Leak or pump failure shows first as pressure loss or delta-P across strainers.

useCases.title: Air Handler Filter Differential Pressure
useCases.value: High ΔP across filters increases fan energy and reduces airflow; indicates change-out due.

useCases.title: Cooling Capacity vs IT Load
useCases.value: Compares available tons to IT heat load (from power meters) to expose margin before next summer.

useCases.title: Economizer Mode Utilization
useCases.value: Low economizer hours may indicate stuck dampers or bad enthalpy programming—wasting energy.

useCases.title: Condensation Risk Alerts
useCases.value: Surface temp below dew point risks water on equipment and slip hazards near chilled doors.

useCases.title: Cooling Redundancy Status
useCases.value: N+1 cooling requires knowing when one CRAC is down and remaining capacity still covers peak IT load.

useCases.title: Data Center Humidity & Condensation Risk
useCases.value: Prevents equipment failure by detecting dew point conditions before condensation forms on servers and network infrastructure.

useCases.title: Water Leak Sensor Zone Correlation
useCases.value: Correlates multiple rope sensors to localize leak source and trigger EPO workflows under raised floor.

useCases.title: Badge Access Audit
useCases.value: Complete badge access audit trail is required for compliance (SOC2, PCI-DSS) and supports security investigations.

useCases.title: After-Hours Access Alerts
useCases.value: Data center access outside business hours requires additional scrutiny. Alerts ensure authorized personnel are verified.

useCases.title: Tailgating Detection
useCases.value: Tailgating bypasses access control, allowing unauthorized entry. Detection supports physical security integrity.

useCases.title: Camera System Health
useCases.value: Offline cameras create security blind spots. Monitoring ensures continuous surveillance coverage.

useCases.title: Cabinet Door Monitoring
useCases.value: Unauthorized cabinet access could indicate tampering. Door sensors provide granular physical security for critical racks.

useCases.title: Fire Suppression and Detection System Alarms
useCases.value: Fire and gas detection events require immediate response. Centralized alarm monitoring ensures rapid escalation and audit trail.

useCases.title: Raised Floor and Cable Management Events
useCases.value: Floor tile removal or cable strain events can indicate unauthorized work or trip hazards. Monitoring supports physical security and change audit.

useCases.title: Data Center Capacity Headroom by Zone
useCases.value: Tracking power, cooling, and space headroom by zone supports capacity planning and prevents over-provisioning in hot spots.

useCases.title: CCTV / IP Camera Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Camera online/offline, storage utilization, recording status ensures continuous surveillance coverage and prevents blind spots during security incidents.

useCases.title: Fire Suppression System Status
useCases.value: Pre-action system armed/disarmed, agent levels (FM-200/Novec) ensure fire suppression readiness; disarmed or low-agent systems leave the data center unprotected.

useCases.title: Environmental Sensor Battery Status
useCases.value: Wireless environmental sensor battery health; dead batteries create monitoring gaps and risk undetected temperature or humidity exceedances.

useCases.title: Badge Tailgating and Anti-Passback Violations
useCases.value: Tracks piggyback events where anti-passback rules fire or two entries occur without intermediate exit—stronger signal than generic door events alone.

useCases.title: After-Hours Access Without Active Work Order
useCases.value: Correlates physical entry with ITSM change/work order to catch unauthorized after-hours presence.

useCases.title: Camera Feed Loss and Recording Gap Detection
useCases.value: Detects loss of RTSP/HLS stream and gaps in NVR recording separately from generic camera “offline” pings.

useCases.title: Visitor Badge Expiry Tracking
useCases.value: Expired visitor badges that remain active create audit findings and tailgating risk.

useCases.title: Cabinet Intrusion and Forced Rack Door Events
useCases.value: Lateral contact/forced-open sensors on colo cabinets detect physical tampering faster than walk-through audits.

useCases.title: Fire Suppression System Health and Supervisory Signals
useCases.value: Supervisory off-normal (low air, pre-action valve trouble) precedes full alarm; distinct from agent level alone.

useCases.title: Access Control Panel Tamper and Line Fault
useCases.value: Enclosure tamper, RS-485 ground faults, or DC line faults may precede bypass or sabotage.

useCases.title: Camera Uptime and Availability Tracking (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Monitors video surveillance system availability to ensure continuous monitoring coverage.

useCases.title: Video Retention and Cloud Archive Storage Utilization (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Tracks cloud storage usage for video archives to manage costs and ensure retention SLA.

useCases.title: Motion Detection Events and Alert Volume Analysis (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Analyzes motion detection event patterns to optimize camera sensitivity and reduce false alerts.

useCases.title: Camera Video Quality Score and Stream Health (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Monitors video quality metrics to identify network or hardware issues affecting video feeds.

useCases.title: Cloud Archive Status and Backup Validation (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Ensures video archives are successfully uploaded to cloud and backup integrity is maintained.

useCases.title: Video Stream Connection Errors and Quality Issues (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Detects video stream connection failures that prevent remote viewing or recording.

useCases.title: Camera Firmware Compliance and Update Management (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Ensures all cameras run current firmware with security patches.

useCases.title: Night Mode Effectiveness and Low-Light Performance (Meraki MV)
useCases.value: Monitors camera performance in low-light conditions to ensure night surveillance effectiveness.

useCases.title: People Counting Trends and Occupancy Analytics
useCases.value: Uses camera people counting to track foot traffic trends for space utilization and facility planning.

useCases.title: Building Occupancy Trending and Capacity Planning
useCases.value: Provides real-time and historical people counts per building, floor, and zone using data from Meraki APs and cameras. Supports compliance with fire safety capacity limits, energy management optimization (HVAC scheduling based on actual occupancy), and real estate planning. Trending data reveals patterns — which floors are overcrowded on Tuesdays, which buildings are underused on Fridays — enabling data-driven workplace strategy decisions.

useCases.title: Visitor Dwell Time and Movement Flow Analysis
useCases.value: Measures how long visitors and employees spend in specific zones and tracks movement patterns between areas. For corporate campuses, this optimizes cafeteria layouts, identifies bottleneck corridors, and improves wayfinding. For retail environments, it measures engagement with displays and optimizes store layouts. For healthcare, it tracks patient flow through departments to reduce wait times. Dwell time analysis reveals which spaces create value and which are passed through without engagement.

useCases.title: Environmental Sensor Monitoring (Temperature, Humidity, Air Quality)
useCases.value: Monitors environmental conditions using Meraki MT sensors — temperature, humidity, air quality (PM2.5, TVOC, CO2), and water leaks. Protects server rooms and network closets from overheating, monitors warehouse cold-chain compliance, detects water leaks before they cause damage, and ensures office air quality meets health standards. Sensor data with five days of onboard storage survives network outages. Threshold-based alerting enables immediate response to environmental hazards.

useCases.title: Asset Tracking and Geofencing Alerts
useCases.value: Tracks the real-time location of high-value assets (medical equipment, network gear, tools, laptops, carts) using BLE tags and Cisco Spaces IoT Explorer. Geofencing alerts notify when assets leave designated zones — preventing theft, loss, and misplacement. In healthcare, this tracks infusion pumps and wheelchairs across departments. In manufacturing, it ensures tools return to storage after shifts. Historical location data supports asset utilization analysis and procurement decisions.

useCases.title: After-Hours Wireless Presence Detection
useCases.value: Detects Wi-Fi-connected devices present in buildings or restricted zones outside of business hours. Correlates with badge access data and employee schedules to identify unauthorized presence — potential tailgating, after-hours theft, or social engineering. Unlike badge-only systems which only detect entry, wireless presence confirms ongoing physical presence. Supports investigations by providing device MAC, location, and duration of after-hours presence. Particularly valuable for facilities with sensitive areas (data centers, labs, executive floors).

useCases.title: Workspace Utilization and Ghost Booking Detection
useCases.value: Combines room booking data with actual physical occupancy from Cisco Spaces and Webex device sensors to calculate true workspace utilization. Identifies "ghost bookings" — rooms reserved but never occupied — which waste available space and frustrate employees searching for rooms. Reveals which rooms are most/least popular, optimal room sizes for actual group sizes, and peak usage patterns. Directly supports real estate cost reduction by providing evidence-based recommendations for space consolidation, redesign, or expansion.

useCases.title: Access Control Event Audit
useCases.value: Physical access logs correlate with logical access events for security investigation. Audit trail required for compliance.

useCases.title: Cisco Spaces Wayfinding and Path Analytics
useCases.value: Understanding how people physically move through a building reveals traffic bottlenecks, dead zones, and inefficient layouts invisible to static occupancy sensors. Cisco Spaces path analytics tracks visitor movement between zones over time — showing that 80% of foot traffic funnels through one corridor, or that a key amenity is consistently bypassed because signage directs people the wrong way. This data drives floor plan optimization, signage placement, and emergency egress planning with evidence rather than guesswork.

useCases.title: Cisco Spaces Proximity and Engagement Analytics
useCases.value: For corporate campuses, retail environments, and visitor centers, understanding how people engage with specific zones — reception desks, demo areas, retail displays, cafeterias, wellness rooms — transforms facility management from guesswork to data-driven optimization. Cisco Spaces dwell time and repeat visit analytics quantify engagement intensity: a demo area where visitors average 30 seconds of dwell time needs redesign, while a breakout space with 45-minute average dwell validates the investment. Repeat visit patterns reveal which spaces become habit destinations vs one-time curiosities.

useCases.title: Cisco Spaces IoT Sensor Alert Correlation with Building Management
useCases.value: Environmental sensor alerts (temperature excursion, humidity spike, poor air quality) are only half the story — the other half is whether the building management system (BMS) responded correctly. Correlating Cisco Spaces IoT sensor alerts with HVAC events, BMS actions, and occupancy patterns validates automated response effectiveness. When a temperature alert fires and the HVAC doesn't respond within 15 minutes, that's an automation failure. When air quality degrades only in occupied zones during peak hours, that's a ventilation capacity issue. This correlation turns isolated alerts into actionable facility intelligence.

useCases.title: Incident Volume Trending
useCases.value: Incident trends reveal infrastructure stability, staffing needs, and the effectiveness of problem management.

useCases.title: SLA Compliance Monitoring
useCases.value: SLA breaches affect customer satisfaction and contractual obligations. Real-time monitoring enables intervention before breaches occur.

useCases.title: MTTR by Category
useCases.value: MTTR per category identifies where process improvements or automation would have the greatest impact.

useCases.title: Change Success Rate
useCases.value: Failed changes are the leading cause of incidents. Tracking success rate drives improvement in change management practices.

useCases.title: Change Collision Detection
useCases.value: Overlapping changes on related systems increase outage risk. Detection enables coordination and conflict resolution.

useCases.title: Problem Trending
